items.title: US corporate profit boom faces its ‘Minsky moment’
items.author: Edward Chancellor
items.creator: Edward Chancellor
items.summary: Earnings for the S&P 500 Index rose 26% in the past year. Tech giants and chipmakers at the heart of the AI boom make up more than half the surge. Depreciation delays and investments in unlisted firms inflate bottom lines. As the economist Hyman Minsky wrote, it cannot last.
items.body:
The artificial intelligence generated by large language models is breathtaking. Equally wonderous is the financial alchemy that accompanies multi-trillion-dollar investments in AI infrastructure. Capital spending is instantaneously transformed into profits, even as the economic viability of the AI buildout remains questionable.
The United States is in the throes of a great profit boom. Corporate profits had reached a record $4.7 trillion for the last twelve months by mid-year. That’s a 17% increase on the previous year’s figures. Tax breaks contained in President Donald Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act have led to a sharp drop in corporate tax receipts. Washington’s enormous fiscal deficit – running at around 6% of GDP – provides an economy wide fillip to corporate bottom lines.
When it comes to individual companies, however, the surge is all about AI. Earnings per share for members of the S&P 500 Index (.SPX) were up 26% in the twelve months to July: the long-run average annual growth rate is 7%. Expected earnings for the third quarter are 35% above estimates from a year ago.
Gerard Minack of Minack Advisors lists 19 members of the S&P 500 that are heavily involved in the AI buildout: Big Tech “hyperscalers”, chipmakers and supply-chain companies such as fibre-optic provider Corning (GLW.N) . Since January 2025, these “AI-19 stocks” have seen forecast earnings rise by around $700 billion, 50% more than all the other companies in the US stock market benchmark.
Analysts at Morgan Stanley predict that 42 leading companies exposed to AI will grow their earnings by 67% in 2026. The aggregate earnings growth of the other S&P 500 companies is projected at 23%. Put another way, these 42 stocks account for more than half of the earnings growth for the S&P 500 in the current year. Next year Morgan Stanley expects the basket of AI plays to contribute 78% of the S&P 500 earnings growth as AI investment in the United States rises to a forecast $1.6 trillion.
“This is the probably the most earnings accretive capex boom in history,” says Jefferies strategist Christopher Wood. AI capital spending inflates profits because, as Minack points out, one company’s capex is another’s revenue. Profits emerge because the investing company does not expense all its costs at once, whereas the seller of capital equipment immediately books the full amount as revenue. Buyers of Nvidia’s (NVDA.O) graphics processing units depreciate their purchases on average over around 6 years, while the chip giant books a juicy upfront profit.
What’s more, when the buyer is acquiring chips for a data centre that is under construction, the depreciation clock does not start ticking until the facility is up and running. Morgan Stanley estimates that as much as 40% of this year’s AI capex will become operational sometime between 2027 and 2029. The earnings mirage will not last indefinitely, though. By the end of the decade, the hyperscalers’ annual depreciation charges will range between $500 billion and $1 trillion, according to a recent report from Capital Gearing Asset Management.
Investments in unlisted AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic are also super-charging profits. Tech giants reflect changes in the private market value of these investments in their earnings statements as “other non-operating income.” In the four quarters leading up to mid-2026, the four major hyperscalers – Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) , and Meta Platforms (META.O) – saw annualized earnings increase by $222 billion while "other non-operating income" rose by $224 billion. In other words, the rising value of unlisted AI investments accounted for all the increase in their reported earnings.
The fact that the AI buildout is increasingly financed with debt adds a further element of instability. The hyperscalers will plough almost all their operating cash flow into capex in the current financial year. These companies have issued around $225 billion of unsecured bonds so far this year, equivalent to around 30% of their full-year capital spending. They also have lease commitments for $1.1 trillion of AI equipment and services, which, since they haven’t yet commenced, are not reported on their balance sheets.
Next year, Morgan Stanley analysts forecast the hyperscalers will have negative free cash flow of around $550 billion. “Access to credit markets and the ability to absorb higher interest rates are fundamental for hyperscalers and neoclouds to be able to deliver against our capex estimates,” says the Wall Street bank. That shouldn’t be too much of a problem for giants like Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon and Meta which enjoy solid credit ratings because of their dominant positions in search, software, online retailing and social media.
The economist Hyman Minsky applied the term “Ponzi finance” to businesses that do not generate sufficient cash flows to meet their outgoings. Loss-making data centre operators and AI frontier labs fit this description. Ponzi finance units, said Minsky, need rising valuations to raise additional capital. When valuations decline and the capital markets seize up, these shaky institutions collapse, causing losses to metastasise through the financial system. That is what happened in early 2000 after the credit markets lost confidence in the debt-fuelled buildout of the information superhighway.
That investors are starting to question the viability of the AI investment splurge should come as no surprise. Productivity improvements from implementing the new technology remain elusive. Rogue AI agents are causing havoc. Models continue to hallucinate. Chinese AI companies are rapidly taking market share from the leading US AI labs.
OpenAI has pushed back its planned IPO while upstart data centre operators such as [USN:L6N45V00W TEXT:"Firmus Technologies"] have shelved their stock offerings. Prospective investors in Anthropic are [USN:L6N46118I TEXT:"weighing a lower valuation"] for the AI company, Reuters reported citing four people familiar with the matter. CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , the largest neocloud, has seen its [USN:L6N46113K TEXT:"shares and bonds tumble"].
The shares of hyperscalers and chipmakers do not look expensive relative to earnings. That’s because the bubble is in profits, not valuations. US homebuilders were in the same position at the peak of the housing bubble in 2006, as were global miners when the commodity supercycle came to a sudden stop in the middle of the last decade. When the AI capex boom ends, earnings growth could revert to trend, says Minack. That moment may come sooner rather than later.

items.title: Five ways to keep safe online in the wake of AI-supercharged hacking
items.author: A.J. Vicens
items.creator: A.J. Vicens
items.summary: Much of the world woke Wednesday to news that PHP, a coding language most people have never heard of but that underlies roughly 70% of all websites, had a hackable vulnerability, sending businesses and governments scrambling to fix it.
items.body:
Much of the world woke Wednesday to news that PHP, a coding language most people have never heard of but that underlies roughly 70% of all websites, had a hackable vulnerability, sending businesses and governments [USN:FWN4661WD TEXT:"scrambling"] to fix it.
While the PHP glitches sit in the underlying code itself, the NSA warned that attackers could use them to take control of web servers to steal data, disrupt services or move through networks on services the average person relies on every day.
Experts say responsibility mostly lies with software providers and organizations that serve customers. But there are basic steps everyone should take to protect themselves.
USE MULTI-FACTOR AUTHENTIFICATION MFA, or multi-factor authentication, requires two forms of verification to access a protected site, such as a password plus a text-based code or security key. Emily Austin, principal security researcher at cybersecurity firm Censys, recommended unique passwords for individual websites, and for people to monitor any transactions.
“But realistically, for situations like the PHP vulnerabilities, there really isn’t much an end user can do beyond hope the services they rely on either don’t use PHP or have people actively working on patching,” Austin said.
The PHP flaws are the latest in a series of severe software bugs made worse by increasingly capable and accessible large language models. Long-hidden flaws in widely used software, once too obscure or complex for humans to exploit, are now much easier to surface and weaponize .
MAKE HARDWARE UPDATES AUTOMATIC Dan Guido, CEO and co-founder of cybersecurity firm Trail of Bits, recommended people “turn on automatic updates for your phone, computer, and home router.” Companies typically issue security updates when patches are available for known vulnerabilities, so installing them promptly limits the window for bad actors.
Even so, consumers remain at the mercy of the services they rely on, Guido said.
“Someone visiting a website can do everything right, like use two-factor authentication, and still have their information exposed,” Guido said. “You can't patch your hospital's website.”
Most of the work falls on companies running services, Guido said. “They need to deploy fixes faster and limit the damage that compromised systems can cause.”
Runa Sandvik, the founder of Granitt and a digital security expert, said people need to update apps and services on their devices whenever they're available, and to not forget about internet-connected devices around the house.
"I can see a scenario in which some people have some sort of IoT device at home that maybe doesn't get frequent updates, maybe doesn't get any updates at all," Sandvik said. "It's worth double checking with the vendor to see if there is anything available."
PATCH, PATCH, PATCH Dr. Daniel Gardham, a lecturer at the Surrey Centre for Cyber Security and the University of Surrey, said organizations must know what software they run, patch promptly and check whether they've already been compromised. In the AI age, attackers have the advantage, Gardham added.
“Finding vulnerabilities is becoming faster and easier, but fixing them across the range of systems that rely on this software is much harder,” Gardham said. “How well organizations manage that gap will determine whether AI makes the internet safer or more vulnerable.”
BEWARE OF SCAMMERS Any time a major cybersecurity threat makes the news, scammers and cybercriminals will try to take advantage, said Nic Adams, co-founder and CEO of 0rcus, a cyberkinetics company.
Be wary of unsolicited links. "When these headlines hit, check the affected company's instructions by opening its app or typing its website address yourself," Adams said. "An urgent message telling you to 'secure your account' deserves extra scrutiny."
YOUR MONEY IS SAFE Banks have been preparing for this moment since frontier models came out, and have "worked extremely hard to ensure there is no more low-hanging fruit for the bad guys to go after," said Paul Benda, executive vice president of risk, fraud and cybersecurity at the American Bankers Association.
However, Benda added, "we are in a new normal" in terms of cyber threats, and consumers need to be aware, especially in the wake of the PHP vulnerabilities, when shopping with random retailers or websites "where their security is not going to be as good as your bank."
Benda said consumers should not reuse passwords across shopping sites, and should consider using passkeys where possible, which are digital keys specific to certain websites, that avoid the need to enter a password into a website and a phishing resistant.
(This story has been refiled to add the dropped words 'unsolicitated links', in paragraph 20.)

items.body:
South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix (000660.KS) has decided not to pursue a US initial public offering of its subsidiary Solidigm, South Korean newspaper Korea Economic Daily reported on Friday, citing unnamed industry sources.
SK Hynix did not have an immediate response to a request for comment.
The news comes weeks after SK Hynix said it was reviewing various options to strengthen Solidigm's competitiveness, but that no decisions had been made.
Solidigm, based in Rancho Cordova, California, is the US-based NAND flash memory and solid-state drive subsidiary of South Korea's SK Hynix Inc.

items.title: Trump administration oversaw 980,000 deportations during first 18 months
items.author: Kanishka Singh
items.creator: Kanishka Singh
items.summary: The US Department of Homeland Security oversaw 980,000 deportations during the first 18 months of President Donald Trump's second term, according to a report published on Thursday in the Migration Policy Institute think tank.
items.body:
The US Department of Homeland Security oversaw 980,000 deportations during the first 18 months of President Donald Trump's second term, according to a report published on Thursday in the Migration Policy Institute think tank.
Only 20% of all deportations in this period involved individuals with a criminal conviction, the report said.
Of deportations of immigrants with two or more years of US residence, 71% were of people who did not have a criminal conviction, it added.
The report was authored by Marc Rosenblum, a former head of the DHS Office of Homeland Security Statistics.
On an annual basis, total deportations are up from the administration of former President Joe Biden and Trump's first term, but remained well below levels routinely observed in the early 2000s, the report said.
Out of the 980,000 Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection deportations during Trump's second term, about 59%, or 580,000, were removals, 30%, or 300,000, were enforcement returns, and 11%, or 110,000, were administrative returns, the report said.
Trump says his immigration crackdown and [USN:L4N3SN13Z TEXT:"deportation drive"] aim to improve domestic security.
Rights advocates say the crackdown has violated due process and free speech rights and has created an unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about [USN:L4N3ZU0AN TEXT:"racial profiling"].
The State Department said on Tuesday the Trump administration has [USN:L1N46613L TEXT:"revoked over 300,000 US visas"] during his second term.
Among visa revocations particularly condemned by rights advocates are those of pro-Palestinian protesters demonstrating against US ally [USN:L6N42U0SO TEXT:"Israel's assault on Gaza"] and of foreigners over [USN:L2N3VV14E TEXT:"social media comments"] about conservative commentator Charlie Kirk's assassination.
The Trump administration's deportation attempts have faced multiple legal challenges with mixed results.

items.title: Venezuelanos se manifestam em todo o país para exigir eleições, no maior protesto contra o governo dos últimos anos
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Milhares de venezuelanos saíram às ruas nesta quinta-feira, no primeiro protesto da oposição em nível nacional em quase dois anos, exigindo eleições livres e outras mudanças políticas.
items.body:
Milhares de venezuelanos saíram às ruas nesta quinta-feira, no primeiro protesto da oposição em nível nacional em quase dois anos, exigindo eleições livres e outras mudanças políticas.
Os Estados Unidos têm trabalhado em estreita colaboração com o governo interino liderado pela presidente interina, Delcy Rodríguez, desde que suas forças capturaram Nicolás Maduro em janeiro.
Tanto o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, quanto Delcy Rodríguez afirmaram que haverá eleições, mas ainda não definiram uma data nem para as eleições legislativas nem para o processo presidencial.
A líder da oposição e ganhadora do Prêmio Nobel da Paz, María Corina Machado, destacou que as eleições devem ocorrer antes de julho de 2027. Seu movimento, Vente Venezuela, organizou o protesto, que ocorreu em Caracas e se repetiu em cidades como Valência, Maracay, San Cristóbal e Maracaibo.
“Vejo isso e fico feliz porque sei que é possível alcançar a mudança”, disse Leosmary Hernández, uma estudante de cosmetologia de 18 anos em Maracay, no Estado central de Aragua.
Nos últimos anos, “passei por tantas coisas ruins, tantos problemas com o dólar, dificuldades para estudar. Tenho grandes expectativas para o meu país, pela nossa próxima governadora, a presidente María Corina”, acrescentou.
O movimento socialista venezuelano — no poder desde 1999, primeiro sob o mandato de Hugo Chávez e, posteriormente, de Maduro — já recorreu, no passado, ao envio de forças de segurança contra manifestantes que denunciavam a repressão política, a inflação galopante e a deterioração dos serviços públicos, entre outros problemas.
O governista Partido Socialista convocou seus simpatizantes a marchar da central Plaza Venezuela, em Caracas, até um ponto próximo ao palácio presidencial, com o objetivo de comemorar o mês da conscientização sobre o câncer de mama.
O ministro do Interior, Diosdado Cabello, conhecido por seus laços estreitos com os serviços de segurança, apareceu na TV estatal participando da marcha. Os simpatizantes da oposição transferiram seu protesto para um local próximo.
As negociações apoiadas pelos Estados Unidos entre uma facção da oposição e o governo interino, que buscam reestruturar a Suprema Corte de Justiça e o Conselho Nacional Eleitoral com o objetivo de garantir a equidade em futuras eleições, realizaram sua última sessão neste mês.
No entanto, as mudanças podem levar bastante tempo. As negociações não incluem o movimento político de Machado, que afirmou que não impedirá seu andamento.
Os manifestantes também exigiram a libertação de pessoas que, segundo afirmam, permanecem detidas por motivos políticos.
A organização de direitos legais Foro Penal, que representa figuras da oposição e outros detidos — muitas vezes sob acusações como a de traição à pátria —, afirma que na Venezuela ainda há mais de 320 presos políticos, apesar das libertações ocorridas este ano no âmbito de uma lei de anistia apoiada pelo Poder Legislativo.
O governo negou repetidamente que mantenha presos políticos e sustenta que a anistia é generosa.

items.title: Brazil's Bradesco meets profit estimates despite slower credit revenue
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Brazilian lender Banco Bradesco on Thursday reported a 14.6% increase in its third-quarter recurring net profit from a year earlier, meeting analysts' expectations despite softer growth in credit-related revenue.
items.body:
Brazilian lender Banco Bradesco (BBDC3.SA) on Thursday reported a 14.6% increase in its third-quarter recurring net profit from a year earlier, meeting analysts' expectations despite softer growth in credit-related revenue.
Bradesco, which kicked off earnings season for large Brazilian lenders, posted a 7.11 billion reais ($1.41 billion) recurring net profit for the July-September quarter, compared with the 7.14 billion reais expected in a LSEG poll of analysts.
CEO Marcelo Noronha said in a statement that Bradesco kept a cautious stance and a moderate appetite for risk amid a challenging macroeconomic environment in Brazil
"We saw slower growth in our credit-related revenues, but this was offset by non-credit revenues and solid cost control," he wrote
Return on average equity (ROAE) rose to 15.6% from 14.7% a year earlier; Bradesco said that, excluding its recent 10 billion-real capital increase, the ROAE would land at 16.1%
The loan book grew 11.1% to 1.15 trillion reais, while the over-90-day delinquency ratio edged up to 4.6% from 4.1%
Provisions for loan losses reached 10.6 billion reais, rising 24.3% year-over-year
The lender kept its 2026 projections unchanged
Bradesco also renewed its share buyback program, with the new program set to start in November spanning up to 106.6 million shares
($1 = 5.0428 reais)

items.title: Sube el canje en Argentina: por qué creció el costo implícito de sacar los dólares del país
items.author: Juan Pablo Álvarez
items.summary: La diferencia entre los dólares implícitos del mercado bursátil había rondando, durante todo el año, entre 3,5 y 4%, pero tuvo un salto en las últimas horas.
items.body: Buenos Aires — La brecha de precios entre el dólar MEP y el dólar contado con liqui (CCL) superó este jueves el 7% y cerró en 5,2%, despegándose de esta forma del nivel que había mantenido a lo largo del año, más cercano a la zona de 3,5% y 4%. En concreto, el costo implícito de dolarizarse en al Bolsa local cerró la rueda en AR$1.549,42, mientras que el cable se ubicó en AR$1.630,81. VER MÁS: Argentina enfrenta una ola de ventas de bonos ante la incertidumbre por las elecciones de 2027 Andrés Azicri, presidente de Vector Investments, explicó que el dólar MEP y el contado con liquidación reflejan dinámicas diferentes. Mientras el primero representa el acceso a dólares dentro del circuito financiero local, el segundo permite transferir divisas al exterior o ingresarlas desde otras jurisdicciones. En ese sentido, señaló que una mayor demanda de CCL en relación con el MEP puede interpretarse como una señal de que más inversores buscan trasladar sus ahorros fuera del circuito local. Sin embargo, advirtió que es difícil identificar con precisión los componentes de esa demanda, ya que las empresas también pueden recurrir al CCL para repatriar fondos a sus casas matrices después de años de restricciones cambiarias. A su juicio, esta diferencia no solo refleja demanda de dolarización, sino también una búsqueda de cambio de jurisdicción. El fenómeno, agregó, suele intensificarse en períodos de elevada incertidumbre política y recordó que la brecha llegó a acercarse al 20% anual antes de las elecciones de 2023. Por su parte, Matías Fernández, líder de research en Aurum Valores, planteó que el aumento del canje puede explicarse por dos factores: una mayor demanda de CCL o la estabilidad del MEP y del tipo de cambio spot como consecuencia de las intervenciones oficiales y de la dinámica del mercado. En su análisis, considera más probable la segunda explicación. Según Fernández, si el mercado cambiario muestra una tendencia alcista, el CCL puede fluctuar con mayor libertad, mientras que el MEP y el tipo de cambio spot están condicionados por la administración de la liquidez y las operaciones y restricciones del Gobierno. Si el spot permanece estable y el MEP acompaña ese movimiento, el CCL puede avanzar y ampliar la diferencia entre ambos dólares financieros. Fernández señaló que la brecha del MEP frente al tipo de cambio spot es menor que hace tres meses, mientras que la del CCL muestra una tendencia alcista. Esa divergencia contribuye a profundizar el canje. En este escenario, las empresas que enfrentan restricciones cambiarias y necesitan dólares pueden recurrir tanto al mercado oficial, a través del Mercado Libre de Cambios (MLC), como al CCL, sin generar necesariamente presiones directas sobre el MEP. VER MÁS: “Resulta ineficiente”: Grupo México explicó por qué no participará de la privatización del Belgrano Cargas Fernández agregó que, si los participantes del mercado esperan que esa dinámica continúe, podría generarse una mayor demanda de CCL ante la expectativa de que su cotización siga subiendo frente a un MEP estable. Aclaró que esta última posibilidad es una hipótesis sobre el comportamiento de los agentes. El movimiento del canje no responde a un desarbitraje puntual, sino a un desbalance estructural entre la oferta y la demanda de dólar cable, según Martín De La Fuente, analista de estrategia de Buenos Aires Valores S.A. (BAVSA). Según detalló, existe una demanda sostenida de la banca privada y de carteras sofisticadas que buscan exposición al exterior, mientras que la oferta proviene principalmente de los dólares que los bancos pueden vender en las licitaciones. A eso se suma un contexto estacional desfavorable, con fondos de Estados Unidos que reducen su exposición al riesgo ante el cierre de sus ejercicios el 31 de octubre, Brasil captando flujos de América Latina en medio de su proceso electoral y US$4.000 millones acumulados en pagos de dividendos y utilidades al exterior durante el año. De La Fuente advirtió que la posibilidad de arbitrar entre el dólar oficial y el CCL es cada vez más restringida, lo que le quita el ancla natural que históricamente permitía cerrar esa brecha. De cara a las próximas semanas, el analista no identifica catalizadores claros para una compresión del canje. Según explicó, la oferta de dólares se moderó tras el pico de septiembre, la demanda preelectoral de cobertura recién empieza a aparecer y la presión para girar divisas al exterior se mantendrá. En ese contexto, De La Fuente consideró que el nivel actual del canje no representa un error de mercado, sino una señal de que la demanda para sacar dólares del país es genuina y creciente. El ejecutivo de BAVSA advirtió que el riesgo es que esta dinámica se retroalimente a medida que se acerque 2027 y la incertidumbre electoral comience a pesar más en las decisiones de cartera.

items.title: The whimsical world of 'Wildwood' comes to life in Laika's most ambitious stop-motion film
items.author: Danielle Broadway
items.creator: Danielle Broadway
items.summary: What began as a visit to a forest on the outskirts of Portland blossomed into the magical world of the stop-motion film "Wildwood," Laika Studios' most ambitious project to date.
items.body:
What began as a visit to a forest on the outskirts of Portland blossomed into the magical world of the stop-motion film "Wildwood," Laika Studios' most ambitious project to date.
"The beginning was this germ of an idea," said Colin Meloy, author of the 2011 novel of the same name on which the film is based.
Meloy imagined Forest Park, a 5,200-acre wooded grassland in Portland, Oregon, as a "magical kingdom" surrounded by an impervious barrier.
The idea led Meloy and his wife, Carson Ellis, who illustrated the novel, to map out the park's boundaries and populate it with mystical creatures and characters, creating the foundation of their fictional world.
"Wildwood," which brings the story from page to picture and arrives in theaters on Friday, follows teenager Prue McKeel, voiced by Peyton Elizabeth Lee, as she ventures into the forest outside Portland after magical crows kidnap her younger brother.
The voice cast also includes Jacob Tremblay as Prue's friend Curtis, Jake Johnson as Mr. McKeel, Prue's father, and Carey Mulligan as the film's antagonist, Alexandra.
"It's really once in a generation they release a movie," Johnson said, referring to Laika.
"When they come out, it means something. It's really special and truly unique," he added.
Laika is known for its handcrafted stop-motion films, combining traditional animation techniques with 3D printing and digital effects. Its 2009 release "Coraline" remains the studio's highest-grossing film and a Halloween cult favorite.
For director Travis Knight, "Wildwood" recalled the fantasy novels he loved growing up, including the works of JRR Tolkien and CS Lewis.
He said the story also had a "weird idiosyncratic voice" that felt uniquely suited to Laika, a Portland-based studio, and to him as a Portland native.
Bringing the story to life in stop-motion proved a major undertaking.
The production used 231 puppets, 54 central hero characters, and 136 locations. Yet animating the puppets to feel lifelike posed an even greater challenge than staging the film's large-scale battle scenes.
"There's a lot of stuff that we did with the puppet department to create breathers in the puppets and muscles," said animation supervisor Brad Schiff.
"So, not only can the animator control them from the outside, but they're also controlling them from the inside, which makes them feel even more alive," he added.

items.title: GM cancels deal with new US rare-earth magnet plant, documents say
items.author: Eric Onstad
items.creator: Eric Onstad
items.summary: General Motors , the biggest customer of a US factory making rare earth magnets for electric vehicles, cancelled its long-term supply deal with the manufacturer, and the two sides are in arbitration, according to regulatory documents and a person with knowledge of the situation.
items.body:
General Motors (GM.N) , the biggest customer of a US factory making rare earth magnets for electric vehicles, cancelled its long-term supply deal with the manufacturer, and the two sides are in arbitration, according to regulatory documents and a person with knowledge of the situation.
The move spotlights the challenges Western firms face in building domestic rare-earths output and cutting their reliance on China, which produces about 90% of global permanent magnets.
It also shows how the US auto industry's landscape has changed since Donald Trump returned to the White House in 2025 and cut federal support for electric vehicles.
Germany's Vacuumschmelze, or VAC, signed a [USN:L8N34F3IX TEXT:"long-term deal"] in 2023 with GM to supply permanent magnets for its electric vehicles from a new plant in South Carolina.
Energy Fuels (UUUU.A) , which agreed in June to pay $1.9 billion to [USN:L4N42V0QM TEXT:"acquire VAC"], said in US Securities and Exchange Commission documents filed last week that a customer of the plant terminated its supply agreement on July 1, and VAC launched arbitration proceedings against that customer several days later.
It did not name the customer, but GM this week reported in an SEC filing that a supplier of a component for EV traction motors "initiated an arbitration against us seeking damages after we terminated a strategic sourcing agreement," without saying why it cancelled the deal.
The person familiar with the matter confirmed GM was the customer that cancelled the contract with VAC's US unit, e-VAC Magnetics.
GM and Energy Fuels declined to comment on the arbitration because it is confidential.
The dispute has not been previously reported and none of the companies involved have issued press releases about the issue.
VAC launched its $500-million US magnet plant late last year with a capacity of just under 2,000 metric tons a year, and 90% was set to be sold to GM, with the remainder supplying the US government, VAC CEO Erik Eschen [USN:L5N3UY0MF TEXT:"told Reuters"] in September last year.
VAC's US unit said it was seeking damages in arbitration due to wrongful termination.
"We have no concerns about VAC’s commercial success and its ability to produce rare earth permanent magnets to customer specifications," Energy Fuels said.
However, Energy Fuels told Reuters there may be "potential adjustments to our purchase price of VAC depending on the outcome of the arbitration."
GM ROLLS BACK EV SALES GM has been pulling back on sales of EVs, which historically have lost money, following the Trump administration’s withdrawal of incentives and tax breaks meant to benefit the industry.
In January, GM took a [USN:L6N3Y915L TEXT:"$6 billion charge"] to unwind some EV investments. When GM and VAC announced the supply deal three years ago, VAC said the plant would support GM for a minimum of 10 years and supply a wide range of models.
The dispute first arose in April 2026, according to the SEC documents. Energy Fuels said it was aware of the dispute when it was negotiating the VAC acquisition.
Energy Fuels, a producer of uranium for the nuclear power industry, said the takeover would allow it to become one of the world's largest non-Chinese producers of magnets used in the aerospace, defence and renewable energy sectors.
VAC supplies magnets to more than 1,000 customers, from facilities in Germany, Malaysia and other countries.

items.title: Venezolanos marchan en todo el país para exigir elecciones, en mayor protesta antigubernametal en años
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Miles de venezolanos salieron a las calles el jueves en la primera protesta de la oposición a nivel nacional en casi dos años, mientras los manifestantes exigían elecciones libres y otros cambios políticos con una presencia notablemente escasa de las fuerzas de seguridad.
items.body:
Miles de venezolanos salieron a las calles el jueves en la primera protesta de la oposición a nivel nacional en casi dos años, mientras los manifestantes exigían elecciones libres y otros cambios políticos con una presencia notablemente escasa de las fuerzas de seguridad.
Estados Unidos ha trabajado estrechamente con el gobierno interino encabezado por la presidenta encargada Delcy Rodríguez, desde que sus fuerzas capturaron en enero a Nicolás Maduro.
Tanto el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, como Rodríguez han afirmado que habrá elecciones, pero aún no han fijado una fecha ni para los comicios legislativos ni para el proceso presidencial.
La líder opositora y ganadora del Premio Nobel de la Paz, María Corina Machado, ha señalado que los comicios deben celebrarse antes de julio de 2027. Su movimiento Vente Venezuela organizó la protesta, que tuvo lugar en Caracas y se replicó en ciudades como Valencia, Maracay, San Cristóbal y Maracaibo.
"Veo esto y me siento feliz porque yo sé que se puede lograr el cambio", dijo Leosmary Hernández, una estudiante de cosmetología de 18 años en Maracay, en el estado central de Aragua.
En los últimos años "he pasado tantas cosas malas, tantos problemas con el dólar, dificultades para estudiar. Tengo unas grandes expectativas para mi país, por nuestra próxima gobernadora, presidenta María Corina", agregó.
El movimiento socialista venezolano —en el poder desde 1999, primero bajo el mandato de Hugo Chávez y posteriormente de Maduro— ha recurrido en el pasado al despliegue de fuerzas de seguridad contra manifestantes que denunciaban la represión política, una inflación galopante, el deterioro de los servicios públicos, entre otros problemas.
El gobernante Partido Socialista convocó a sus simpatizantes a marchar desde la céntrica Plaza Venezuela de Caracas hacia un punto cercano al palacio presidencial, con el fin de conmemorar el mes de la concienciación sobre el cáncer de mama.
El ministro del Interior, Diosdado Cabello, conocido por sus estrechos vínculos con los servicios de seguridad, apareció en la TV estatal participando en la marcha. Los simpatizantes de la oposición trasladaron su protesta a un lugar cercano. Rodríguez envió un mensaje a los participantes de la manifestación a través de una llamada divulgada por la televisora estatal.
Las conversaciones respaldadas por Estados Unidos entre una facción de la oposición y el gobierno interino, que buscan reestructurar el Tribunal Supremo de Justicia y el Consejo Nacional Electoral con el fin de garantizar la equidad en futuras elecciones, celebraron su última sesión este mes. Sin embargo, los cambios podrían llevar bastante tiempo.
Rodríguez tenía previsto reunirse en el palacio de gobierno con Dinorah Figuera, la jefa de la delegación opositora en las conversaciones apoyadas por Washington, según imágenes de la televisora estatal mostrando la llegada de Figuera a la sede oficial.
Las negociaciones no incluyen al movimiento político de Machado, quien ha manifestado que no obstaculizará su avance.
"Queremos elecciones presidenciales ya, que se haga un cronograma ya. No vamos a esperar hasta 2028", dijo María Débora Marín, de 57 años, quien regenta una tienda de ropa en el centro de la ciudad de Valencia, a unos 150 kilómetros al sur de Caracas, al referirse a versiones de que las elecciones podrían celebrarse recién dentro de dos años. "Lo que queremos es avanzar, salir ya de esta pesadilla", agregó.
En estos momentos "estamos en un limbo", comentó Rayeska Puesme, de 18 años y recién graduada, mientras participaba en la protesta en Caracas, añadiendo que ha considerado marcharse de Venezuela debido a la falta de oportunidades. "Estados Unidos saco un gran problema, que fue Maduro, pero falta el resto", añadió. "Siento en mi corazón que las cosas van a cambiar, pero no veo cuándo", dijo.
Los manifestantes también exigieron la liberación de personas que, según afirman, permanecen detenidas por motivos políticos.
La organización de derechos legales Foro Penal, que representa a figuras de la oposición y a otros detenidos —a menudo bajo cargos como el de traición a la patria-, afirma que en Venezuela todavía hay más de 320 presos políticos, a pesar de las liberaciones que tuvieron lugar este año en el marco de una ley de amnistía respaldada por el poder legislativo.
El gobierno ha negado reiteradamente que mantenga a presos políticos y sostiene que la amnistía es generosa.

items.title: Tesouro dos EUA retira Venezuela da lista de países sujeitos a restrições aos investimentos dos EUA no exterior
items.author: Andrea Shalal
items.creator: Andrea Shalal
items.summary: O Departamento do Tesouro dos EUA anunciou nesta quinta-feira uma proposta de regulamentação para a análise de investimentos no exterior na China, na Rússia e em outros países — uma lista que não inclui mais a Venezuela, agora que o ex-presidente do país Nicolás Maduro não está mais no poder.
items.body:
O Departamento do Tesouro dos EUA anunciou nesta quinta-feira uma proposta de regulamentação para a análise de investimentos no exterior na China, na Rússia e em outros países — uma lista que não inclui mais a Venezuela, agora que o ex-presidente do país Nicolás Maduro não está mais no poder.
O Tesouro aceitará comentários até 7 de dezembro sobre as regras propostas, que foram determinadas pela Lei Abrangente de Segurança Nacional para Investimentos no Exterior de 2025 (COINS Act), aprovada pelo Congresso em dezembro, mas que surgiu de um esforço bipartidário iniciado pelo ex-presidente Joe Biden em 2023.
A Lei COINS marcou uma expansão significativa dos controles sobre os investimentos externos dos EUA, exigindo que empresas e indivíduos norte-americanos notifiquem o Tesouro sobre certos planos de investimento, ao mesmo tempo em que os proíbe totalmente em outros casos para evitar danos à segurança nacional dos EUA. Ela ampliou a lista de países abrangidos e incluiu a biotecnologia como um dos setores restritos, conferindo ao Tesouro a autoridade para adicionar outros setores conforme necessário.
O programa de investimentos no exterior tinha inicialmente como alvo apenas a China, mas a legislação COINS ampliou a lista de países “motivos de preocupação” para incluir Cuba, Irã, Coreia do Norte, Rússia e Venezuela “sob o regime de Nicolás Maduro”.
Mas o Tesouro afirmou que retirou a Venezuela da lista, uma vez que o governo Maduro “não existe mais” após a captura do ex-presidente por forças norte-americanas em janeiro, acrescentando que o atual governo, liderado pela vice de Maduro, Delcy Rodríguez, não se enquadrava na definição. A regra proposta ainda poderia se aplicar a certos investimentos em entidades venezuelanas, afirmou o Tesouro, sem dar mais detalhes.
O presidente Donald Trump recebeu o presidente chinês Xi Jinping para uma luxuosa visita de Estado a Washington no mês passado e tem adotado uma abordagem menos restritiva em relação às tecnologias chinesas em seu segundo mandato, mas a divulgação, nesta quinta-feira, das regras propostas pode sinalizar um desejo de manter alguma pressão sobre as ambições tecnológicas de Pequim.
“A ideia por trás do programa de investimentos no exterior é garantir que tenhamos a capacidade de monitorar e, potencialmente, proibir os tipos de investimentos” que representam riscos à segurança nacional dos EUA, disse à Reuters o secretário-adjunto do Tesouro, Chris Pilkerton, responsável por questões de segurança de investimentos.
“Não se trata apenas do investimento em si; não se trata apenas do dinheiro. Trata-se da rede, da cadeia de suprimentos e de aspectos como esses que decorrem desse investimento”, disse ele, acrescentando que uma teia tão complexa de relações seria difícil de regulamentar de outra forma, por meio de controles de exportação ou outras medidas.
O Tesouro afirmou que as regras propostas não proibiriam todos os investimentos em países que suscitam preocupação. Em vez disso, elas visariam investimentos específicos em entidades envolvidas em tecnologias de dupla utilização que beneficiem programas militares, Estados de vigilância e países com violações dos direitos humanos.
As regras propostas exigem notificação sobre investimentos potenciais em seis setores e cinco países designados, ao mesmo tempo em que os proíbem totalmente no caso da inteligência artificial.

NEW YORK: US stocks tumbled on Thursday (Oct 22) and the Nasdaq posted its steepest daily drop since early June as a batch of high-profile earnings reports ignited fresh fears about the AI spending race.
The S&P 500 ended deep in negative territory. But the tech-laden Nasdaq , dragged down by microchips, suffered a steeper loss, falling 2.6 per cent in the wake of a spate of high-profile AI-related earnings results.
The blue-chip Dow eked out a nominal gain minutes before the closing bell.
Meta Platforms' results beat analyst expectations, but its stock slid 7.0 per cent as the Facebook parent posted its first cash outflow in more than a decade due to its AI-related expenditures and announced plans to issue non-voting shares in a two-for-one split to raise capital to spend on the nascent technology.

Tesla shares fell 3.1 per cent even though the electric car maker unexpectedly posted positive free cash flow in the quarter and cut its 2026 capital spending plans.
The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index .SOX , which has driven much of the current bull market's gains, plunged 6.7 per cent , its biggest daily percentage drop since June 23.
With Thursday's decline, the SOX is off more than 26 per cent from its record closing high reached on Jun 22, yet it remains up 51.5 per cent so far this year. The S&P 500 has risen 11.9 per cent over the same period.
"It's a wonderful day on Wall Street," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser & market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois. "The only part of the market that is really suffering here is technology, which has been the golden child of the markets up until about June."
"Investors are starting to realize that there are some holes in the AI story," Nolte added. "And that's having an impact on the indices because they're so heavily weighted toward technology."
On the geopolitical stage, Iran-backed Houthis launched new strikes against Saudi targets, sending crude prices to a five-month high. Investors worried that ongoing Middle East strife could keep inflation hot and force the US Federal Reserve to keep raising interest rates.
Data from the Labour Department showed initial claims for unemployment benefits kept drifting along near multi-decade lows. Signs of labor market stability will allow the Fed to focus on fighting inflation. Financial markets are currently pricing in the probability that the central bank will raise its policy rate by another 25 basis points before year-end.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI rose 11.89 points, or 0.02 per cent, to 52,867.98, the S&P 500 .SPX lost 93.74 points, or 1.21 per cent, to 7,663.43 and the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC lost 694.00 points, or 2.60 per cent, to 26,008.86.

NEW YORK: US stocks tumbled on Thursday (Oct 22) and the Nasdaq posted its steepest daily drop since early June as a batch of high-profile earnings reports ignited fresh fears about the AI spending race.
The S&P 500 ended deep in negative territory. But the tech-laden Nasdaq , dragged down by microchips, suffered a steeper loss, falling 2.6 per cent in the wake of a spate of high-profile AI-related earnings results.
The blue-chip Dow eked out a nominal gain minutes before the closing bell.
Meta Platforms' results beat analyst expectations, but its stock slid 7.0 per cent as the Facebook parent posted its first cash outflow in more than a decade due to its AI-related expenditures and announced plans to issue non-voting shares in a two-for-one split to raise capital to spend on the nascent technology.

Tesla shares fell 3.1 per cent even though the electric car maker unexpectedly posted positive free cash flow in the quarter and cut its 2026 capital spending plans.
The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index .SOX , which has driven much of the current bull market's gains, plunged 6.7 per cent , its biggest daily percentage drop since June 23.
With Thursday's decline, the SOX is off more than 26 per cent from its record closing high reached on Jun 22, yet it remains up 51.5 per cent so far this year. The S&P 500 has risen 11.9 per cent over the same period.
"It's a wonderful day on Wall Street," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser & market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois. "The only part of the market that is really suffering here is technology, which has been the golden child of the markets up until about June."
"Investors are starting to realize that there are some holes in the AI story," Nolte added. "And that's having an impact on the indices because they're so heavily weighted toward technology."
On the geopolitical stage, Iran-backed Houthis launched new strikes against Saudi targets, sending crude prices to a five-month high. Investors worried that ongoing Middle East strife could keep inflation hot and force the US Federal Reserve to keep raising interest rates.
Data from the Labour Department showed initial claims for unemployment benefits kept drifting along near multi-decade lows. Signs of labor market stability will allow the Fed to focus on fighting inflation. Financial markets are currently pricing in the probability that the central bank will raise its policy rate by another 25 basis points before year-end.

items.title: Britain to use military aircraft to fight climate change-fuelled wildfires
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Britain said on Thursday it would for the first time use military helicopters and aircraft to fight wildfires after its hottest summer on record, as the government steps up efforts to combat a threat it says is being fuelled by climate change.
items.body:
Britain said on Thursday it would for the first time use military helicopters and aircraft to fight wildfires after its hottest summer on record, as the government steps up efforts to combat a threat it says is being fuelled by climate change.
The Royal Air Force's Chinook helicopters and A400M transport aircraft to be equipped with wildfire firefighting capability.
The military aircraft are to be available to support emergency services battling blazes in remote areas.
Government to provide up to £45 million ($60.15 million) for specialist response teams and firefighter equipment.
Government to invest £25 million in peatland restoration and support farmers to reduce wildfire risk.
New AI unit to be established to help predict and track wildfires.
Government to work with the Met Office, Britain's national meteorological service, to improve wildfire forecasting and risk assessment.
($1 = 0.7482 pounds)

items.title: Samarco eleva produção em 4% no 3º tri e atinge maior nível desde retomada
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A mineradora Samarco, joint venture da Vale com a BHP, produziu 4,3 milhões de toneladas de pelotas e finos de minério de ferro no terceiro trimestre, alta de 4% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025 e de 10% ante o segundo trimestre deste ano, segundo prévia operacional divulgada nesta quinta-feira.
items.body:
A mineradora Samarco, joint venture da Vale com a BHP, produziu 4,3 milhões de toneladas de pelotas e finos de minério de ferro no terceiro trimestre, alta de 4% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025 e de 10% ante o segundo trimestre deste ano, segundo prévia operacional divulgada nesta quinta-feira.
O volume representa o maior nível trimestral desde a retomada das operações da companhia, ao final de 2020, cerca de cinco anos após o desastre envolvendo a queda de uma barragem de rejeitos de mineração.
Nos nove primeiros meses de 2026, a produção alcançou 12 milhões de toneladas, avanço de 7% na comparação anual e também o maior volume para o período desde a retomada operacional.
Segundo a Samarco, o desempenho reflete a manutenção de níveis elevados de produção ao longo do ano.
As vendas de pelotas e finos somaram 3,9 milhões de toneladas entre julho e setembro, em linha com o trimestre anterior, mas com queda de 5% na comparação anual. No acumulado de 2026, as vendas atingiram 11,0 milhões de toneladas, crescimento de 1% sobre os nove primeiros meses de 2025.
O preço médio realizado de pelotas foi de US$125,1 por tonelada no período, praticamente estável em relação ao segundo trimestre e 4% superior ao registrado um ano antes.
Segundo a companhia, o resultado refletiu melhores condições comerciais e a recuperação dos prêmios de pelotas ao longo do trimestre.

items.title: Your guide to open enrollment season
items.author: Lauren Young
items.creator: Lauren Young
items.summary: I sat down this week to sign up for my 2027 benefits.
items.body:
I sat down this week to sign up for my 2027 benefits.
Ouch. My premiums will rise by 8%.
Amid [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"higher inflation"], rising healthcare costs are definitely taking a bite out of budgets. While there is not much we can do about higher premiums, one area where we do have some agency is flexible spending accounts.
Figuring out how much to put into your account is always tricky. For example, most of my New York-based doctors do not accept health insurance. (I pay out of pocket and submit for reimbursement.)
About 4 in 10 flexible spending account holders forfeited unused funds in 2024, according to new research from the Employee Benefit Research Institute. Those who forfeited funds returned an average of $404 to their employers.
If you don’t get healthcare from your employer and buy it on the open marketplace, enrollment for US plans also starts on November 1 . But higher premiums already pushed some consumers away.
Affordable Care Act and other individual health insurance plan enrollment fell 18% to 20.5 million members in June, [USN:L1N4600RY TEXT:"according to health policy research firm KFF"], marking the steepest annual decline since 2015 as Americans struggle with rising health insurance costs.
One other item of note: More companies are dropping coverage of weight-loss drugs from their insurance plans. The culprit? [USN:L1N44L0V0 TEXT:"Once again, it’s rising costs"].
How is all of this impacting you? If you are picking benefits, use a flexible spending account, take weight-loss drugs or buy your own coverage, tell me how you plan to shop this year via the link in my bio.
READ. WATCH. LISTEN. [USN:L6N46012F TEXT:"End of an era? How the Hermes Birkin bag is losing its scarcity appeal "]
Ahead of the US midterms, Gen Z investors are making portfolio changes
[USN:L6N45Z0WG TEXT:"Fed sees AI boom adding to inflation headache, but others may pay for the medicine "]
Can prediction markets help us understand the future?
[USN:L4N45K10K TEXT:"Beauty giants target 'Ozempic face' as boom in obesity drugs opens new market"]
Are higher prices the new normal?
How to give your kids money for a house without things getting weird
Consumers are under pressure. Here is why that’s bad for the economy
GIMME CREDIT What kind of benefits are you getting from your credit cards? I’m a big fan of racking up miles on my card for airline upgrades as well as priority boarding.
According to a 2026 survey by Citizens Financial Group, 44% of Gen Z and 19% of millennials reported that credit card rewards have made a significant difference for their households, whether by helping offset costs, access experiences or get more value from their cards.
Here is the story of how one young consumer is using the rewards from four credit cards to get a bigger bang from his spending.
Do you maximize your credit card rewards? If so, how? Let me know the scoop via the link in my bio.
THE CRYPTO COUPLE What happens when love and digital portfolios merge?
I recently profiled a couple who met on a Discord server, fell in love while trading crypto tips and ultimately decided to build a portfolio — as well as a family — with digital currencies.
Their story interested me because study after study shows financial literacy is sexy, including this one by crypto exchange OKX , which found that 66% of Americans believe knowledge of personal finance makes someone more attractive.
Digital-asset fluency carries weight, too: 55% of men and 49% of women said that understanding digital assets makes someone more desirable, the OKX survey found.
What do you think? Is fiscal fitness attractive? Tell me what you think via the link in my bio.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Aditya Soni

[２２日　ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）の安全性を研究する非営利団体ＭＥＴＲとレッドウッド・リサーチは、今年実施したパイロットレビューで、
items.body:
Aditya Soni

[２２日　ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）の安全性を研究する非営利団体ＭＥＴＲとレッドウッド・リサーチは、今年実施したパイロットレビューで、 ＡＩ開発企業オープンＡＩの内部システムに複数の新たな脆弱性を発見した。その中には、エージェントが数百回に及ぶ自らの行動を監視対象から外すために利用できた可能性のあるものも含まれていた。

ＭＥＴＲとレッドウッドは２２日、この検証は７月２１日から８月１１日にかけて実施され、「組み込み型評価」と呼ばれる手法に基づき、外部の研究者らにオープンＡＩの内部インフラへの「高度なアクセス権限」が与えられたと説明した。 

両団体はそれぞれ研究者１人を派遣し、オープンＡＩの内部コード、ドキュメント、および一部の技術スタッフへのアクセスを許可する体制を検証。いずれの研究者も現場で付き添いを受け、オープンＡＩから支給された「構内から持ち出し禁止」のデバイスを使用した。

研究者らは、オープンＡＩの「Ｃｏｄｅｘ」エージェントがセキュリティー上の制限を回避し、ユーザーの完全な権限で動作する潜在的な経路があることを特定した。また、監視システムについて、７月２１日時点およびそれ以前の状態を評価対象としたと説明し、評価期間中にもオープンＡＩが同システムを拡張していたと指摘した。 

オープンＡＩは両団体に対し、本番環境の安全対策に影響する脆弱性は全て修正済みだと伝えた。一方、両団体は修正内容を検証していないとしている。 

オープンＡＩは「今回の調査結果は、システムを拡張する過程で安全対策を強化するのに役立ち、ＭＥＴＲや他の第三者評価機関との今後の研究協力の在り方を形作る上で一助となるだろう」と述べた。

items.title: Putin says talks must focus on security for Russia, Ukraine and Europe overall
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that future talks on a settlement of the war in Ukraine should focus on security guarantees for both countries and an overall framework for security throughout Europe.
items.body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that future talks on a settlement of the war in Ukraine should focus on security guarantees for both countries and an overall framework for security throughout Europe.
Putin, interviewed on Russian television a day after meeting US presidential envoy Steve Witkoff, confirmed that Russia was ready to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine next month.
He restated longstanding Kremlin policy that Russia never wanted to launch a war, but had run into hostile reactions from Ukraine on key issues of concern to Moscow.
Talks on a variety of matters could lead to a positive outcome, he said, but Russia remained intent on a solution ending the conflict rather than a short-lived ceasefire.
"The goal of these talks will be to ensure the security of Ukraine and Russia after reaching peace agreements, in their final form, not as a result of a temporary ceasefire for some short period of time. We are ready to resume these contacts to achieve this goal," Putin said.
The Russian president said Witkoff also stressed that discussions had to extend to "the architecture of European security as a whole. And I agree with that too. Well, let's see how things develop in the coming days."
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who met Witkoff in Norway on Tuesday, said Ukraine was [USN:L1N4670ZQ TEXT:"ready for talks"] likely to take place by early next month. Ukraine, he said, supported "any proposals for a ceasefire, an end to the war, an energy ceasefire as well as humanitarian initiatives".
Efforts headed by the United States to pursue talks stalled in February with the outbreak of the US-Israeli conflict with Iran.
Many of the Ukraine war issues focus on territory, with Russia demanding Ukraine cede all of eastern Ukraine's Donbas region. Kyiv rejects any notion of giving up land it currently holds.
In his comments, Putin said any discussion on territory in eastern Ukraine had to consider what he said was the fact that the area was "historically Russian land".
And residents there, he said, had voted to be a part of Russia in referendums staged seven months after Moscow launched its invasion.
"Firstly, my attitude on this matter is that this is not their territory. It’s the territory of historical Russia," he said.

items.title: Brandon Woodruff recovery leaves Brewers with tough call before Game 1
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: MILWAUKEE -- After almost a decade as a franchise cornerstone, Milwaukee Brewers right-hander Brandon Woodruff hopes his comeback from his latest injury leads to a spot on the club's 2026 World Series roster.
items.body:
MILWAUKEE -- After almost a decade as a franchise cornerstone, Milwaukee Brewers right-hander Brandon Woodruff hopes his comeback from his latest injury leads to a spot on the club's 2026 World Series roster.
But the team's current longest-tenured player also knows that it may be beyond his control, depending on MLB postseason roster rules.
Woodruff, who underwent shoulder surgery during the 2025 season, has not pitched since July 4 after experiencing another issue with his shoulder. Woodruff was initially scheduled for season-ending surgery, but that was canceled when he showed signs of improvement.
He began a throwing program in late August and threw off a mound during each of the Brewers' first two postseason series. He threw about two dozen live pitches Tuesday to teammates.
"It went as good as it could have gone," Woodruff said Thursday. "And I've probably made their decision a little bit harder, which is a good problem for them. So, I'm lucky, I'm blessed. We got a chance to win the World Series and regardless of what happens, I will be just as excited to win if I'm on the roster or not."
MLB rules say that a player on a postseason roster can be replaced only if he suffers an acute, non-chronic injury or ailment. If Woodruff were to suffer another injury, the Brewers are not sure if it would be considered recurring or pre-existing, which would prevent them from replacing Woodruff on the World Series roster.
Several reports indicate the Brewers have discussed the situation with MLB.
"We have a decision to make," Brewers president of baseball operations Matt Arnold said Thursday. "Still going to spend some minutes talking about him and again the rest of our group there."
"This is a guy that's one of the most successful, dominant big-game pitchers I've ever been around, and there are also some rule constraints that we're having to work through with the health, etc., that have to be a consideration because he hasn't pitched in a game since July 4," Arnold said.
Woodruff, 33, is 55-30 with a 3.10 ERA since debuting with the Brewers in 2017. At the end of last season, he took a $10 million buyout after declining his half of a mutual option, but then accepted the Brewers' $22.025 million, one-year qualifying offer.
Woodruff made six starts in March and April this season before going on the injured list with right shoulder inflammation. In his first start back on June 22, he allowed one hit over six scoreless innings with 10 strikeouts in a no-decision against the Cincinnati Reds. The Brewers won 2-1 in 10 innings.
In his third start after returning, he exited after allowing three runs in 3 2/3 innings against the Arizona Diamondbacks on July 4. There was a noticeable drop in his velocity.
Brewers manager Pat Murphy said that he obviously would like to have Woodruff on the roster, but he balances that desire with what gives the club the best chance to win.
"Now he's got a clean bill of health according to the trainers, but if that same injury comes up again, then we can't replace him," Murphy said. "So those are the things we've got to weigh heavily. What is he going to give us? We'd love to do it. It's a great story. But we have responsibility to those 20-some guys in there and to the organization and to the city and to whoever else we're responsible to."
For Woodruff, his first World Series opportunity after nine seasons is down to wait and see.
"I just wanted to be an option at this point," Woodruff said. "I know what I bring to the table as a player and I'll always believe in myself. But I also realized that I haven't pitched in a game in three months or whatever it is. So, there's definitely a lot that goes into the decision. I haven't heard anything yet. I'm sure they're going to talk about it obviously through (Thursday)."
--Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

items.title: Venezuelans call for elections in first national protest in nearly two years
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Thousands of Venezuelans took to the streets on Thursday in the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years, as demonstrators demanded free elections and other political changes with a notably thin presence of security forces.
items.body:
Thousands of Venezuelans took to the streets on Thursday in the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years, as demonstrators demanded free elections and other political changes with a notably thin presence of security forces.
The United States has been working closely with the interim government led by acting President Delcy Rodriguez since US forces captured President Nicolas Maduro in January. Both US President Donald Trump and Rodriguez, Maduro's former deputy, have said there will be elections, but have not set a date either for a legislative vote or a national contest for president.
Opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize winner Maria Corina Machado, who has been outside the country for nearly a year after living in hiding following a contested 2024 election, has said elections must take place by July 2027.
Her Vente Venezuela movement organized the protest, which took place in the capital Caracas and other cities, including Valencia, Maracay, San Cristobal and Maracaibo.
“Seeing this makes me happy because I know change is possible," said 18-year-old cosmetology student Leosmary Hernandez, as she gathered with hundreds of others in northern Maracay. "I’ve been through so many hardships, so many problems because of the dollar, and difficulties studying. I have high hopes for my country and for our next leader, president, Maria Corina."
"I went out to protest before, when things were much tougher, and I’m even less afraid today because I want my voice to be heard,” she added as music boomed around protesters waving Venezuelan flags.
Venezuela's socialist movement, in power since 1999 under late President Hugo Chavez and then Maduro, has in the past [USN:KBN1DU1MZ TEXT:"deployed security forces against protesters"] decrying political repression, dizzying inflation, poor public services and other problems in the economically battered country, including after the 2024 presidential election.
Security forces had minimal presence at protest sites on Thursday, and in many smaller cities demonstrators dispersed before dark.
The ruling Socialist Party called for its supporters to march from Caracas' Plaza Venezuela, the same place the opposition planned to gather two hours later, to a location near the presidential palace to commemorate Breast Cancer Awareness Month.
Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello, known for his close ties to the security services, was pictured on state television attending the march, while the opposition supporters moved their protest to a nearby location.
NEGOTIATIONS CONTINUE US-backed talks between a faction of the opposition and the interim government, aimed at remaking the top court and the electoral council with an eye toward ensuring fairness at eventual elections, held their latest session this month, but changes could [USN:L1N45G0XU TEXT:"take significant time"]. The negotiations do not include Machado's political movement, though she has said she will not stand in the way of their progress.
Machado's proxy roundly won the 2024 election according to vote tallies released by the opposition. But the government, which never released full counts, backed Maduro, as did the country's legal and electoral institutions.
"We want presidential elections now. We want an electoral timetable to be announced now. We are not going to wait until 2028," said Maria Debora Marin, 57, who runs a clothing store in central Valencia, referring to rumors elections may only take place the year after next. "What we want is to move forward and finally get out of this nightmare."
Amid the arrests of some of her closest collaborators, Machado went into hiding. Her last [USN:L1N3O40ZB TEXT:"public appearance in Venezuela"] was at protests to mark Maduro's third inauguration in January 2025, where she was briefly detained.
Machado has for years sought US support, [USN:L4N3W51LU TEXT:"aligning with hawks"] in the Trump team who argued that Maduro — through links to drug gangs — represented a direct threat to US national security. Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, are facing [USN:L6N46017G TEXT:"drug and torture charges"] in the US. They have pleaded not guilty.
But Trump has repeatedly praised Rodriguez's management and her willingness to [USN:L6N46308A TEXT:"welcome US investors"], saying last month it is too soon to consider elections.
Machado's desire to return home, especially after [USN:L6N43414H TEXT:"devastating twin earthquakes"] in June, has caused [USN:L1N42Y0X4 TEXT:"friction in Washington"], with US officials asking her to delay her trip, Reuters has reported.
"We're in limbo," said recent graduate Rayeska Puesme, 18, as she attended the protest in Caracas, adding she had considered leaving because of a lack of opportunities. "The United States removed one big problem, which was Maduro, but the rest are still there."
"I feel in my heart that things are going to change, but I don't see when."
Demonstrators were also calling for the release of prisoners they say are held for political reasons.
Legal rights group Foro Penal, which represents opposition figures and others who have been detained, often on charges like treason, says there are still more than 320 political prisoners in Venezuela, despite releases that took place under an amnesty law backed by the legislature earlier this year. The government has repeatedly denied holding political prisoners and says the amnesty is generous.
items.raw_description: Thousands of Venezuelans took to the streets on Thursday in the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years, as demonstrators demanded free elections and other political changes with a notably thin presence of security forces.

items.title: Bradesco tem lucro líquido de R$7,1 bi no 3º tri, aprova recompra de ações
items.author: Paula Arend Laier
items.creator: Paula Arend Laier
items.summary: O Bradesco teve lucro líquido recorrente de R$7,1 bilhões no terceiro trimestre, alta de 14,6% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, em linha com as previsões no mercado, com o presidente-executivo do banco, Marcelo Noronha, apontando um mercado de crédito mais restrito, com a taxa de juros em nível elevado e desaceleração da economia.
items.body:
O Bradesco (BBDC3.SA) teve lucro líquido recorrente de R$7,1 bilhões no terceiro trimestre, alta de 14,6% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, em linha com as previsões no mercado, com o presidente-executivo do banco, Marcelo Noronha, apontando um mercado de crédito mais restrito, com a taxa de juros em nível elevado e desaceleração da economia.
O banco também anunciou um novo programa de [USN:L1N4681ED TEXT:"recompra"] de ações envolvendo 3,55% das ações ordinárias e aproximadamente 1% dos papéis preferenciais em circulação. O Bradesco também afirmou que aprovou R$4,1 bilhões em juros sobre capital próprio aos acionistas no terceiro trimestre.
"É cenário desafiador para todos", afirmou o executivo em comunicado à imprensa, após a divulgação do balanço nesta quinta-feira. "Vimos nossas receitas relacionadas a crédito crescerem menos, mas conseguimos compensá-las com receitas não oriundas de crédito e bom controle de despesas”, acrescentou. Na comparação trimestral, o lucro do Bradesco subiu apenas 0,8%.
A carteira de crédito da instituição totalizou R$1,15 trilhão no final de setembro, aumento de 11,1% ano a ano, mas de apenas 1,1% em relação ao final de junho. O índice de inadimplência acima de 90 dias no terceiro trimestre ficou em 4,6%, de 4,1% um ano antes e 4,3% no segundo trimestre de 2026. O custo do crédito, representado pela despesa de provisões (PDD) expandida, cresceu 24,3% ano a ano e 6,6% na comparação trimestral, para R$10,6 bilhões.
O banco atribuiu a "leve alta" na inadimplência acima de 90 dias no trimestre ao segmento de micro, pequenas e médias empresas (MPME), particularmente nas operações de capital de giro com garantia do Governo Federal, afirmando que os atrasos desse produto corresponderam a cerca de metade da evolução da inadimplência total. Também destacou atrasos sazonais nas operações do Banco John Deere, que pressionaram os indicadores de pessoas físicas.
Na movimentação da carteira de crédito por estágios, o montante no estágio 1, considerado com risco saudável, de até 30 dias, somava R$730,8 bilhões, enquanto no estágio 2, que mostram aumento de risco, com atrasos entre 31 e 90 dias; totalizava R$46,7 bilhões e no estágio 3, que indica problemas de recuperação de crédito; alcançava R$62,5 bilhões.
No segundo trimestre do ano, esses valores eram R$727,3 bilhões, R$46 bilhões e R$60,2 bilhões, respectivamente.
CONTROLE DE DESPESAS No terceiro trimestre, o retorno sobre o patrimônio líquido médio (ROAE) ficou em 15,6%, de 14,7% no mesmo intervalo do ano passado e 16,2% no segundo trimestre do ano. Desconsiderando o [USN:L1N45O0VZ TEXT:"aumento de capital"] de R$10 bilhões homologado no começo de outubro, o ROAE foi de 16,1%.
O aumento de capital ajudou na melhora dos índices de capital do banco. O Bradesco encerrou o terceiro trimestre com índice de Basileia total de 16% e de capital principal de 12,1%. Um ano antes esses percentuais eram 15,9% e 11,4%, respectivamente. Em junho, eram 15,5% e 11,3%.
As receitas totais do banco somaram R$38 bilhões, alta de 8,4% ano a ano, com a margem financeira total somando quase R$21,4 bilhões, expansão de 14,2% na mesma base de comparação. A margem com clientes cresceu 10,1%, para 20,5 bilhões, enquanto a margem com mercado alcançou R$875 milhões, de R$99 milhões um ano antes. As despesas operacionais recuaram 1%. O índice de eficiência ficou em 45,4%, de 50,1% no mesmo período do ano passado.
Ao final de setembro, o banco tinha uma rede com 1.741 agências, além de 723 unidades de negócios e 1.428 postos de atendimento. Em junho, eram 1.844 agências, além de 698 unidades de negócios e 1.565 postos de atendimento.
O resultado do grupo segurador do Bradesco mostrou lucro líquido recorrente de R$2,9 bilhões, alta de 14,1% ano a ano, com ROAE de 22%.

items.title: Ator Tom Skerritt, protagonista de “Alien” e “Top Gun”, morre aos 93 anos
items.author: Will Dunham
items.creator: Will Dunham
items.summary: O versátil ator Tom Skerritt, que estrelou grandes sucessos de Hollywood, incluindo o clássico de ficção científica “Alien”, a comédia de guerra “M.A.S.H” e o drama de ação “Top Gun”, faleceu aos 93 anos, confirmou seu empresário.
items.body:
O versátil ator Tom Skerritt, que estrelou grandes sucessos de Hollywood, incluindo o clássico de ficção científica “Alien”, a comédia de guerra “M.A.S.H” e o drama de ação “Top Gun”, faleceu aos 93 anos, confirmou seu empresário.
Natural de Detroit, Skerritt, cuja carreira em Hollywood se estendeu da década de 1960 até a década de 2020, faleceu na quarta-feira de causas naturais, informou a ABC7, citando um comunicado da família do ator.
Conhecido por sua beleza rude e pela capacidade de se destacar em diversos gêneros, Skerritt desempenhou atuações memoráveis em papéis principais e coadjuvantes no cinema e na televisão.
O papel que marcou a carreira de Skerritt foi o de um cirurgião rebelde do Exército dos EUA na comédia de humor negro “M.A.S.H”, de 1970, do diretor Robert Altman, sobre a Guerra da Coreia -- filme cujo elenco também contava com Donald Sutherland, Elliott Gould e Sally Kellerman. Skerritt interpretou o sulista Duke Forrest enquanto os médicos do Hospital Cirúrgico Móvel do Exército atendiam soldados feridos.
O filme, cuja popularidade coincidiu com o mal-estar dos norte-americanos em relação à Guerra do Vietnã, foi indicado a cinco prêmios do Oscar.
No claustrofóbico filme de ficção científica e terror “Alien”, de 1979, dirigido por Ridley Scott, Skerritt interpretou Dallas, o capitão de uma nave espacial malfadada cuja tripulação se depara com uma criatura extraterrestre parasita mortal, de aparência surrealista e atitude hostil. Em uma das cenas mais famosas e sangrentas do filme, o personagem de Skerritt está sentado ao lado de seu colega de elenco John Hurt quando um bebê alienígena sai violentamente do torso do personagem de Hurt.
“Alien”, uma obra-prima influente cujo elenco também contava com Sigourney Weaver e Ian Holm, recebeu duas indicações ao Oscar.
“São a espontaneidade e o impulso que fazem a diferença, e foi isso que senti que tivemos em ‘Alien’. Cada um de nós tinha essa sintonia imediata uns com os outros -- o respeito que eu tinha pelos outros atores e o respeito que eles tinham por mim”, disse Skerritt ao entrevistador Peter Sobczynski em 2019, ao mesmo tempo em que elogiava a genialidade de Scott como diretor.
“Alien” foi um dos vários filmes em que Skerritt atuou e que apresentavam personagens femininas fortes, neste caso a corajosa Ripley, interpretada por Weaver. Isso foi considerado pioneiro na época.
“Quando li o roteiro, uma das coisas que mais gostei foi que a mulher se torna a heroína. Adorei isso”, disse Skerritt.
“Ver mulheres em posições de força e determinação para estabelecer as conexões certas e tomar as decisões corretas foi o que me atraiu. Eu também vivenciei isso em ‘Flores de Aço’, com as mulheres daquele filme. Gostei da ideia de mulheres serem duronas, fortes e influentes.”
Em “Flores de Aço” (1989), Skerritt interpretou Drum Eatenton, marido de M’Lynn Eatenton, personagem de Sally Field.
Tony Scott, irmão do diretor de “Alien”, escalou Skerritt para o importante papel coadjuvante do instrutor da aviação naval Viper Metcalf no sucesso de bilheteria de 1986 “Top Gun”, que ajudou o astro Tom Cruise a alçar voo rumo à estratosfera de Hollywood.
Skerritt também interpretou o marido de Shirley MacLaine no drama de balé “Momento de Decisão”, de 1977, dirigido por Herbert Ross, e contracenou com outra estrela em ascensão, Brad Pitt, no drama de época “Nada É Para Sempre”, de 1992, dirigido por Robert Redford e com belíssimas imagens.
Entre outros filmes em que atuou, destacam-se: “Ensina-me a Viver” (1971), “Castelos de Gelo” (1978), “Na Hora Da Zona Morta” (1983), “Poltergeist 3 - O Capítulo Final” (1988), “Contato” (1997), “Lágrimas do Sol” (2003) e “Ted” (2012).
Nascido em 25 de agosto de 1933, em Detroit, Skerritt serviu na Força Aérea dos Estados Unidos antes de se tornar ator, fazendo sua estreia no cinema em 1962 ao lado de um jovem Redford em “Obsessão de Matar”. Ele era pai de cinco filhos e se casou três vezes.
