items.title: 14 Indians on boat attacked near Bab el-Mandeb? Houthis blame Saudi Arabia, claim rescue operation
items.author: Ravi Hari
items.summary: The latest developments come after renewed clashes between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis ended a United Nations-brokered truce that had largely halted cross-border attacks since 2022, opening another front amid the wider US-Israeli war on Iran.
items.body: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group is rescuing a boat carrying 14 Indian nationals that was attacked off Jabal Zuqar island near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the group’s military spokesperson Yahya Saree said on Thursday (October 22), blaming Saudi Arabia for the incident.The development comes amid escalating hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, with attacks targeting Saudi energy infrastructure and airports. India has strongly condemned the continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including the October 21 strikes on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oil field in the Eastern Province.Saudi authorities did not immediately respond on the alleged boat attack. The circumstances of the incident were not independently established in the information available.India condemns attacks on Saudi energy infrastructureIn a statement, India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said the attacks on Saudi Arabia had resulted in civilian deaths and injuries.“One Indian national unfortunately died and two others were injured in the attack on Dammam airport, while another Indian national was injured in the attack on the Shaybah oil field,” the ministry said.The MEA conveyed its condolences to the family of the Indian national killed in the Dammam airport attack and wished those injured a speedy recovery. It added that the Indian Embassy in Riyadh was in contact with Saudi authorities and would provide all possible assistance.India also called for an immediate halt to attacks on civilian and critical infrastructure, describing them as “completely unacceptable”. It said it stood in solidarity with the people and government of Saudi Arabia in safeguarding the kingdom’s sovereignty and expressed hope that peace and normalcy would return to the region.Aramco asks staff to evacuate Dhahran headquartersSeparately, Saudi state oil giant Saudi Aramco has instructed employees to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran and work remotely, Reuters reported, citing six people with knowledge of the matter.The instruction follows a wave of Houthi attacks targeting the kingdom, including Saudi energy facilities and airports. The reason for the evacuation was unclear, and Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment.The Houthis have claimed responsibility for attacks on Aramco facilities in the Red Sea city of Yanbu and the Saudi defence ministry in Riyadh. Saudi authorities have not confirmed the reported strikes.The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted drones over Riyadh and Medina on Thursday. Earlier, a Houthi attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on Wednesday evening killed two people, including an Indian national, and injured eight others, according to the report. Saudi aviation authorities said airport operations had resumed and air traffic had returned to normal.The renewed fighting has also raised concerns about oil supplies. Saudi Arabia’s benchmark stock index fell 2.5% on Thursday, according to LSEG data, while oil prices rose to their highest levels since May amid fears of further escalation in the Middle East.Indian Embassy issues safety advisoryThe Indian Embassy in Riyadh had earlier urged Indian nationals in Saudi Arabia to remain calm and vigilant amid the evolving security situation.In its October 13 advisory, the embassy asked Indians to stay indoors in the event of an aerial attack and follow instructions issued by local authorities through official channels. It also advised them against circulating or reposting videos or news related to the ongoing events.The embassy said it had opened a 24-hour control room to assist Indian nationals and urged travellers to remain in regular contact with their airlines and verify flight updates before travelling.The embassy also said Indian nationals whose visit, tourist, Umrah or business visas had expired because they were unable to leave due to flight unavailability would be permitted to exit Saudi Arabia without paying fines, according to information provided by Saudi authorities.(With Reuters inputs)

items.title: Trump invokes Cold War-era Defense Production Act for oil production, refining
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: US President Donald Trump determined on Thursday that petroleum production, refining, and related activities are essential to national defense, a move that could open up US funding for fossil fuel projects.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump determined on Thursday that petroleum production, refining, and related activities are essential to national defense, a move that could open up US funding for fossil fuel projects.
In a presidential memo, Trump also invoked part of the Cold War-era Defense Production Act, allowing him to provide financial incentives for oil-related activities, pipelines and storage of liquid fuels.
Prices for crude oil and [USN:L6N45Z19G TEXT:"diesel"] have surged since the US and Israel attacked Iran in joint action at the end of February. Since then, the conflict has limited energy shipments globally, with Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries exacerbating the fuel shortages.
The surge in costs poses a risk for Trump in the November 3 elections, as his fellow Republicans try to maintain control of both chambers of Congress. The Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll that closed Monday shows [USN:L6N465159 TEXT:"just 36% of Americans"] approve of Trump's handling of the economy.
The memo said that without taking the actions, the US is not able to provide enough of those energy services in a "timely manner due to constrained financing, long lead times, permitting and infrastructure bottlenecks, and supply chain limitations."
The memo did not mention specific projects that could be funded. The US averaged around 13.6 million barrels of daily crude production in 2025, making it the largest crude producer worldwide.
Last week, Vice President [USN:L6N45Z1BU TEXT:"JD Vance said"] the administration would use the Defense Production Act to expand capacity of a Texas refinery owned by Delek US Holdings (DK.N)
Trump signed legislation last year that included $1 billion in Defense Production Act funding for energy-related projects deemed critical to national security.
items.raw_description: US President Donald Trump determined on Thursday that petroleum production, refining, and related activities are essential to national defense, a move that could open up US funding for fossil fuel projects.

items.title: Steelers scrap Paris fan event as Saints game proceeds despite protests
items.author: Vincent Daheron, Amy Tennery
items.creator: Vincent Daheron, Amy Tennery
items.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers cancelled a weekend fan event in Paris on Thursday as French authorities prepared for fresh protests ahead of the NFL's first regular-season game in the capital.
items.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers cancelled a weekend fan event in Paris on Thursday as French authorities prepared for fresh protests ahead of the NFL's first regular-season game in the capital.
France experienced some of its worst urban unrest in years [USN:L8N4670KY TEXT:"last weekend"], prompting President Emmanuel Macron to tighten curbs on protests [USN:L6N4680S7 TEXT:"on Thursday"], amid fears that demonstrations planned for Saturday could turn violent.
The Steelers face the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis on Sunday, around 10 kilometres from the Place de la Bastille, where Saturday's protests are expected to begin.
The Steelers informed fans on Thursday that a "Steelers House" fan event in the Bastille neighbourhood would not go forward.
"The NFL, as they do for every game, including international games, is working closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. As stated by the NFL, there have been no disruptions or impacts at League sites," the team said in a statement.
"As a precautionary measure, the Steelers designated bar that had been planned in Bastille – an area that has experienced recent disruptions – will not proceed."
The Saints were practising this week in Versailles after arriving in France on Monday, while the Steelers were reportedly travelling to Paris on Thursday evening.
"A lot of planning, a lot of extra conversations," Steelers coach Mike McCarthy told reporters on Wednesday. "Just because all the state of what surrounds the game."
The French Interior Ministry was due to hold a press conference on Friday to outline security measures for the protests on Saturday.
NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell told reporters on Wednesday that he had been in contact with the US Secretary of State regarding security plans.
"We're continuing to make sure we have all available information, make sure the appropriate steps are being made," said Goodell. "We're guests in the country. We're going to be good guests."
The Paris game is one of a record nine international contests for the NFL this season, as the league looks to capitalise on lucrative overseas markets.
League officials sought to ease concerns at a two-day owners meeting in New York this week, and [USN:L6N46612U TEXT:"told reporters"] that staging the game would not divert local security forces from other duties.

items.title: Tesoro retira a Venezuela de lista de países sujetos a restricciones inversión EEUU en el extranjero
items.author: Andrea Shalal
items.creator: Andrea Shalal
items.summary: El Departamento del Tesoro anunció el jueves una propuesta de normativa para controlar las inversiones en China, Rusia y otros países, una lista en la que no aparece Venezuela ahora que el expresidente Nicolás Maduro ya no está en el poder.
items.body:
El Departamento del Tesoro anunció el jueves una propuesta de normativa para controlar las inversiones en China, Rusia y otros países, una lista en la que no aparece Venezuela ahora que el expresidente Nicolás Maduro ya no está en el poder.
La Ley Integral de Seguridad Nacional en materia de Inversiones en el Extranjero de 2025 (COINS Act), aprobada por el Congreso en diciembre, supuso una ampliación significativa de los controles sobre las inversiones en el extranjero al exigir a las empresas y particulares que notifiquen al Tesoro determinados planes de inversión.
Amplió la lista de países afectados e incluyó la biotecnología como uno de los sectores restringidos, otorgando al Tesoro la autoridad para añadir sectores adicionales según sea necesario.
El programa de inversiones en el extranjero se centraba inicialmente solo en China, pero la legislación COINS amplió la lista de países "que suscitan preocupación" para incluir a Cuba, Irán, Corea del Norte, Rusia y Venezuela "bajo el régimen de Nicolás Maduro".
Sin embargo, el Tesoro afirmó que había excluido a Venezuela debido a que el Gobierno de Maduro "ya no existe", añadiendo que el Gobierno de la presidenta encargada Delcy Rodríguez no se ajustaba a la definición. La norma propuesta podría seguir aplicándose a determinadas inversiones en entidades venezolanas, señaló el Tesoro, sin dar más detalles.
El presidente Donald Trump ha adoptado un enfoque menos restrictivo respecto a las tecnologías chinas en su segundo mandato, pero la publicación el jueves de las normas propuestas podría indicar un deseo de mantener cierta presión sobre las ambiciones tecnológicas de Pekín.
El Tesoro señaló que las normas propuestas no prohibirían todas las inversiones en países que suscitan preocupación. En cambio, se centrarían en inversiones específicas en entidades dedicadas a tecnologías de doble uso que beneficien a programas militares, a Estados que practican la vigilancia y a países donde se cometen abusos contra los derechos humanos.
El Tesoro añadió un sector adicional —la biotecnología— a los cinco identificados en la legislación: semiconductores avanzados y microelectrónica; sistemas de inteligencia artificial; tecnologías de información cuántica; computación de alto rendimiento y supercomputación; y sistemas hipersónicos.
Señaló que ciertas biotecnologías avanzadas podrían suponer un grave riesgo para la seguridad nacional, citando la proliferación de armas biológicas, el desarrollo de interfaces cerebro-ordenador y el perjuicio para la seguridad de la cadena de suministro de EEUU.
Las normas no incluyen los posibles acuerdos de licencia celebrados por empresas farmacéuticas estadounidenses con China, afirmó un responsable del Tesoro, lo que satisface una exigencia clave de grandes fabricantes de medicamentos como Pfizer (PFE.N) .

items.title: US Democratic senator probes Ukraine's loss of Starshield service
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Democratic US Senator Richard Blumenthal on Thursday said he had opened an inquiry into Ukraine's loss of critical access to the Pentagon's Starshield satellite communications service and the resulting degrading of Kyiv's ability to defend itself against Russian attacks.
items.body:
Democratic US Senator Richard Blumenthal on Thursday said he had opened an inquiry into Ukraine's loss of critical access to the Pentagon's Starshield satellite communications service and the resulting degrading of Kyiv's ability to defend itself against Russian attacks.
"In the late evening of October 13, Ukrainian forces lost critical access to Starshield, the military-grade counterpart to SpaceX’s Starlink network, after their access to speeds at which equipment could stay connected to the network was capped," Blumenthal wrote in a letter to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
"The episode raises urgent questions about who possesses the technical and legal authority to alter these capabilities" and whether the Pentagon has "sufficient alternatives" if SpaceX-provided services become unavailable, Blumenthal wrote.
Blumenthal is the senior Democrat on the Senate's Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. He is seeking information on whether the change in service was [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"directed by the White House"], the Department of Defense or SpaceX.
Republicans control the Senate, so Democrats lack subpoena power. Blumenthal can only request information and briefings from officials within and outside the government.
He said the move put Ukrainian forces and civilians at risk and raised concerns "about who controls critical capabilities the US government has spent billions of dollars to procure."
WEAKENED UKRAINE DEFENSES The Pentagon is the biggest customer of Starshield, which is the military-grade version of the Starlink service.
A Pentagon spokesperson said: "As with all congressional correspondence, the Department will respond directly to the authors."
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy on October 14 said Elon Musk's SpaceX had [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"restricted Starlink services"], weakening Ukraine's air defenses.
The controversy came as the Trump administration was pressuring Kyiv to halt its attacks on Russian energy infrastructure and encouraging Russia to return to negotiations over ending its war in Ukraine.
Blumenthal told Hegseth the Senate panel will look into government interactions with and reliance on SpaceX technology. He set deadlines of November 5 for responses to questions embedded in the letter to Hegseth, and November 12 for a briefing by SpaceX officials with knowledge of the Starshield restriction.
Besides this latest inquiry, Blumenthal has been trying to investigate [USN:L6N45E0PR TEXT:"a series of actions related to the Trump administration"], including contracts negotiated for building a White House ballroom at an estimated cost of $400 million and Trump-linked crypto firms.
If Democrats win control of the Senate in November 3 midterm elections, he likely would become chairman of the investigations panel.

items.title: US Treasury drops Venezuela from countries facing outbound US investment restrictions
items.author: Andrea Shalal
items.creator: Andrea Shalal
items.summary: The US Treasury Department on Thursday announced proposed rules for screening outbound investment in China, Russia and other countries, a list that no longer includes Venezuela now that the country's former president Nicolas Maduro is not in power.
items.body:
The US Treasury Department on Thursday announced proposed rules for screening outbound investment in China, Russia and other countries, a list that no longer includes Venezuela now that the country's former president Nicolas Maduro is not in power.
Treasury will accept comments through December 7 on the proposed rules, which were mandated under the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025, or COINS Act, that [USN:L1N3XN0X2 TEXT:"passed Congress in December"], but grew out of a bipartisan effort first begun under former President Joe Biden in 2023.
The COINS Act marked a significant expansion of US outbound investment controls, requiring US firms and individuals to notify Treasury about certain investment plans while banning them outright in other cases to prevent harm to US national security. It expanded the covered countries and added biotechnology as one of the restricted sectors, giving Treasury the authority to add additional sectors as needed.
The outbound program initially targeted China alone, but the COINS legislation expanded the list of countries "of concern" to include Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela "under the regime of Nicolas Maduro."
But Treasury said it dropped Venezuela since Maduro's government "no longer exists" following the capture of the former president by US forces in January, adding that the current government, led by Maduro's deputy, Delcy Rodriguez, did not meet the definition. The proposed rule could still apply to certain investments in Venezuelan entities, Treasury said, without elaborating.
President Donald Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping for a lavish state visit to Washington last month, and has pursued a less restrictive approach on Chinese technologies in his second term, but Thursday's release of the proposed rules may signal a desire to keep some pressure on Beijing's tech ambitions.
"The idea behind the outbound program is to ensure that we have the ability to monitor and potentially prohibit the types of investments" that pose risks to US national security, Treasury Assistant Secretary Chris Pilkerton, who oversees investment security issues, told Reuters.
"It's not just about the investment itself; it's not just about the money. It's about the network, the supply chain, and things like that that come from that investment," he said, adding that such a complex web of relationships would be hard to regulate otherwise through export controls or other measures.
Treasury said the proposed rules would not ban all investments in countries of concern. Instead, they would target specific investments in entities that engaged in dual-use technologies that benefited military programs, surveillance states and countries with human-rights abuses.
The proposed rules require notification about prospective investments in six sectors and five designated countries, while banning them outright in the case of artificial intelligence.
They allow certain exceptions, including investments in publicly traded companies and transactions valued at less than $50,000. The proposal would also allow investors to request exemptions for transactions deemed to be in the national interest of the United States, Treasury said.
Treasury also added an additional sector -- biotechnology -- to the five identified in the legislation: advanced semiconductors and microelectronics; artificial intelligence systems; quantum information technologies; high-performance computing and supercomputing; and hypersonic systems.
It said certain advanced biotechnologies could pose an acute risk to national security, citing the proliferation of biological weapons, the development of brain-computer interfaces and harm to US supply chain security.
The rules do not include potential licensing agreements made by [USN:L1N4570SO TEXT:"US pharmaceutical companies "]with China, a Treasury official said, meeting a key demand of major drugmakers like Pfizer (PFE.N) .
The proposed rules ban investments in artificial intelligence technologies in the target countries. Treasury said it decided on the ban given rapid advances over the past two years that raised questions about the efficacy of "regulating or even distinguishing the most advanced models."

items.title: カナダとトルコ、戦略的パートナーシップ締結　ＦＴＡ交渉開始へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Maria Cheng　Tuvan Gumrukcu

[アンカラ　２２日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Maria Cheng　Tuvan Gumrukcu

[アンカラ　２２日　ロイター] - カナダのカーニー首相は２２日、トルコを初めて公式訪問し、エルドアン大統領と貿易・投資、防衛・安全保障、エネルギー、社会・外交関係を柱とする新たな戦略的パートナーシップに署名した。両国は来月に自由貿易協定（ＦＴＡ）交渉を開始することでも合意。カーニー氏は「新たな世界秩序」の中でトルコとの関係を前進させる必要性に言及し、米国への依存を減らすため新たな貿易相手国の開拓を進める取り組みを続けたい考えだ。

カーニー氏はエルドアン氏との共同記者会見で「労働者や企業に新たな機会を生み出し、カナダとトルコ両国の国民に大きな安全と繁栄をもたらす、戦略的パートナーシップという新たな種をまいた。注意深く取り組み、強い意思を持って育てていけば、何世代にもわたって発展していく」と述べた。

エルドアン大統領も「長年続いてきたトルコとカナダの断絶が解消された。両国は今、新たな時代をスタートさせる」と表明。両国間の貿易額を現在の３０億ドルから、まず５０億ドル、最終的には１００億ドルへ拡大する考えを示した。ただ、時期については言及しなかった。

カナダとトルコが署名した新たな戦略的パートナーシップは、両国の企業のビジネス拡大を通して雇用や経済機会の創出を目指すもので、４本の柱で構成され、３年間の行動計画が盛り込まれている。アンカラで行われた式典で両国の閣僚がエネルギー、防衛、航空輸送分野での協力協定に署名した。エネルギー分野では、原子力、重要鉱物、液化天然ガス（ＬＮＧ）などの分野で協力を強化する。

カーニー氏によると、カナダとトルコの交渉担当者は来月、アンカラで自由貿易協定（ＦＴＡ）交渉の初会合を開く。このほか、カナダ輸出開発公社（ＥＤＣ）とトルコ輸出入銀行（エクシムバンク）が、第三国での事業で両国企業の協力を促進するための新たな協定に署名する。

カーニー氏は記者会見で、「断絶」や「新たな世界秩序」の中でトルコとの関係を前進させる必要性に言及。ただ、カーニー氏もエルドアン氏も米国に直接言及することはなかった。

カーニー氏は２１―２３日の日程でトルコを訪問。２３日にはイスタンブールでトルコの主要企業幹部や投資家との会合に出席する。

items.title: Australia weigh changes for Cape Town decider after South Africa rout
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Australia will have some hard decisions to make over the weekend as they lick their wounds after a bruising loss in the second test against South Africa and consider their line-up for the series-deciding clash next week.
items.body:
Australia will have some hard decisions to make over the weekend as they lick their wounds after a bruising loss in the second test against South Africa and consider their line-up for the series-deciding clash next week.
Defeat by an innings and 31 runs in Gqeberha has left several players’ places in jeopardy and given the selectors plenty to ponder before the third test starts in Cape Town on Tuesday.
Australia are not known for making knee-jerk changes after a defeat, and captain Pat Cummins was circumspect on the topic after the loss at St George’s Park.
"It's always that delicate balance," he said of a potential switch in personnel.
"Do you feel like someone's just about to turn the corner and they're going to be away? Or does it now feel like the right time for change? So that's what will be spoken about in the next few days.
"We'll probably have Cam Green and Josh Inglis available for next week. I'm sure their names will get thrown around when we try to work out an eleven," he told reporters on Thursday.
The debate is likely to include Marnus Labuschagne, who has scored 37 twice, 14 and 39 in his four innings in the two tests in South Africa this month. He has not made a test century since scoring 111 against England at Old Trafford in July 2023.
"The hardest thing about opening or batting No. 3 is actually getting yourself in. So he's actually doing the hard bit. He's getting to thirties," Cummins added.
"He's got to find a way to turn those into bigger scores. Thirties aren't going to win you too many matches.
"It's certainly not a technique error. It's maybe some decisions where the game demands something a little bit different. We'll work on that. He's hitting the ball well,” added the skipper.
CHANGE IN BATTING ORDER There is likely to be a shift in the batting order with Matt Renshaw fancied to return to the top in place of Nic Maddinson, allowing Green to return from an abdominal strain. Josh Inglis and Cooper Connolly are also options.
"Looking around the changing room at how good our batters are and the standards they all hold themselves to, I think we're probably a little bit short of where we'd like to be. We've got three or four days to get it right for Cape Town. There'll be lots of conversations."
Veteran spinner Nathan Lyon could also be recalled, depending on conditions, leaving Australia to decide how to accommodate Scott Boland, who took five wickets in the test and produced a heroic effort with the bat as he offered some second-innings resistance on Thursday.
"We clearly need to be a lot better than that if we want to compete,” Cummins added.
“I think a loss can sometimes kick you into gear. You can maybe paper over the cracks sometimes in a win. Whereas I think in a loss, it makes you ask questions as a player of yourself."

items.summary: A wave of worry around AI and tech crashed over global markets on Thursday, slamming equities and bond yields as investors sought the refuge of US Treasuries, while a spike in Brent crude oil to a five-month high and continued unrest in France also deepened the gloom.
items.body:
A wave of worry around [USN:L6N468196 TEXT:"AI and tech"] crashed over global markets on Thursday, slamming [USN:L6N4680M6 TEXT:"equities"] and bond yields as investors sought the refuge of US Treasuries, while a spike in Brent crude [USN:L6N4671H6 TEXT:"oil "]to a five-month high and continued unrest in [USN:L6N4680QK TEXT:"France "]also deepened the gloom.
In [USN:L6N46713L TEXT:"my column today"], I look at whether the US Treasury will reduce the size of 20-year bond auctions, or soon scrap them all together. Interest payments are high, Treasury wants to shorten the maturity of the debt, and the 20-year part of the curve is relatively illiquid. Absent concerted fiscal tightening, Treasury may have to tinker round the edges if it wants to lower long-term yields. This could help.
Today's Key Reads
[USN:L6N468080 TEXT:"Millions of hacking attempts as companies, governments rush to patch PHP flaws "]
[USN:L6N468116 TEXT:"French bond pain puts euro zone's weak links on notice "]
[USN:L6N45Y119 TEXT:"Investors see risk from US midterms to AI trade as data center backlash builds "]
[USN:L6N4671AG TEXT:"Musk's political baggage clouds prospects for SpaceX-Tesla deal"]
[USN:L6N46718F TEXT:"Surging sterling shakes off Britain's budget blues: Mike Dolan "]
Today's Key Market Moves
STOCKS: South Korea -3.5%, China -2%, Japan -2.5%. [USN:L6N4680I3 TEXT:"Europe "]has biggest fall in 3 weeks. Nasdaq -2.6%, biggest fall since June 5 and sheds $1 trillion of market cap.
SECTORS/SHARES: Five sectors on the S&P 500 fall, six rise. Tech -3%, utilities +2%. Philadelphia Semiconductor Index -6.7%. [USN:L1N46813Q TEXT:"Moderna "]-18%, Amazon, Nvidia -4.5%. [USN:L4N4680UW TEXT:"Blackstone "]+8%, [USN:L4N46720Z TEXT:"P&G"] +5.6%
FX: [USN:L1N468013 TEXT:"Japanese yen, Swiss franc"] the biggest G10 FX gainers. Norwegian crown also up strongly. Bitcoin -4%, biggest fall since June.
BONDS: [USN:L6N4680QK TEXT:"French/German"] 10y spread 175 bps, widest since 2011. US yields sink as much as 20 bps across the curve. 5-year TIPS auction soft - lowest bid/cover since April last year, highest yield in three years.
COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L6N4671H6 TEXT:"Oil "]up as much as 4%, Brent highest since May above $112. [USN:L4N46801E TEXT:"Gold "]-2%, lowest in more than two months.

Today's Talking Points:
Call security
Investors' AI fears ramped up on Thursday, and not just for the usual concerns around spend, revenue and valuations. On top of all that, the global scramble by companies and governments to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet in response to millions of hacking attempts is a reminder of how vulnerable the world is to cybersecurity breaches and AI going rogue.
When governments take websites offline as an emergency precaution, you know it's serious. "I've not seen anything like this in a long, long time," Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said. The good news is these flaws appear to have been flagged by AI before any serious or lasting damage could be wrought. The iShares Cybersecurity and Tech ETF (with the appropriate ticker symbol ) rose on Thursday, bringing its year-to-date gains up to nearly 50%.
Play it safe
There's been a lot of talk this year that the assets investors typically turn to in periods of market turbulence - particularly US Treasuries and other sovereign bonds - have lost their safe-haven allure. They are no longer the hedge or portfolio diversifier they used to be. There is probably some truth to that, but there's life in the old dogs yet.
German bund yields had their biggest drop since May last year, and the Japanese yen and Swiss franc were the two biggest climbers in global FX markets on Thursday. The move in US Treasuries was extraordinary, as yields plunged across the curve and by as much as 20 basis points. And that was despite Brent oil spiking to $112 a barrel. Granted, gold fell, but when was the last time gold truly behaved like a "safe haven"?
Bearing up
China's stock market fall on Thursday means the blue-chip CSI300 index is now down more than 20% from its most recent closing peak on June 22. That's a bear market. Others might argue Chinese stocks have been in a bear market for nearly two decades, since the all-time high reached in 2007. But however you slice it, investing in China has been challenging, to put it mildly.
The currency is rising and is now at a four-year high, while the 10-year bond yield is hovering around its all-time low below 1.60%. But the domestic woes of debt, deflation and depressed consumption weigh heavily. Foreign investment [USN:P8N42P008 TEXT:"flows"] into China in January-September fell 4.3% year-on-year to 548.8 billion yuan ($82.2 billion), the commerce ministry said on Thursday, while outbound non-financial direct investment totaled $101 billion. Export inflows are booming, investor inflows, not so much.
What could move markets tomorrow?

UK retail sales (September)
European Central Bank board members Piero Cipollone and Patrick Montagner speak at separate events
Canada retails sales (August)
US University of Michigan inflation expectations, consumer sentiment (October, final)

items.title: FCC grants Intel waiver for foreign-made robotic devices
items.author: David Shepardson
items.creator: David Shepardson
items.summary: The Federal Communications Commission said on Thursday it has granted a waiver to Intel from its ban on some foreign-made advanced robotics.
items.body:
The Federal Communications Commission said on Thursday it has granted a waiver to Intel (INTC.O) from its ban on some foreign-made advanced robotics.
The FCC said it would grant a one-year waiver of its rules in order to prevent "potential disruptions in the availability of domestic semiconductor manufacturing services for Intel’s customers."
Intel in a petition last week said the robotic devices are critical to its US semiconductor manufacturing. Without the waiver, Intel would not have been allowed to make software, firmware, and hardware changes for its "Automated Guided Vehicles" that it said could be classified by the agency as robots.
Intel told the FCC there is a lack of proven domestic alternatives that meet operational requirements and replacing the automated guided vehicles would take Intel years and could disrupt its manufacturing operations.
The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The vehicles are used to transport materials within Intel's semiconductor facilities and have been in operation for over two decades, the company said.
In July, the FCC barred imports of new Chinese robots and power inverters, seeking to protect the US AI buildout from national security threats and reshore key industries slated for explosive growth.
The FCC barred imports of new Chinese humanoid and quadruped robots, in addition to connected power inverters. The FCC has since granted some approvals to allow for continued specific robotic device imports.
Some analysts forecast broad adoption of humanoid robots, topped with AI-enabled "brains," in consumer and industrial arenas, while explosive data-center construction in the US will depend on reliable sources of inverters.

items.title: Vacina contra câncer da MSD/Moderna reduz em 42% risco de morte ou recorrência do melanoma
items.author: Julie Steenhuysen, Michael Erman
items.creator: Julie Steenhuysen, Michael Erman
items.summary: A Moderna e a MSD anunciaram nesta quinta-feira que sua vacina contra o câncer baseada em mRNA, quando combinada com a imunoterapia amplamente utilizada pela MSD, reduziu em 42% o risco de morte ou recorrência do melanoma em um grande estudo clínico, abrindo potencialmente caminho para uma nova era de tratamento personalizado.
items.body:
A Moderna (MRNA.O) e a MSD (MRK.N) anunciaram nesta quinta-feira que sua vacina contra o câncer baseada em mRNA, quando combinada com a imunoterapia amplamente utilizada pela MSD, reduziu em 42% o risco de morte ou recorrência do melanoma em um grande estudo clínico, abrindo potencialmente caminho para uma nova era de tratamento personalizado.
As ações da Moderna dispararam desde que as empresas anunciaram, em agosto, o sucesso do estudo sem apresentar os dados reais, quase quadruplicando até o fechamento da quarta-feira. Elas fecharam com queda de mais de 17% após os resultados terem vazado em um site de oncologia na manhã desta quinta-feira. As ações da MSD fecharam com queda de cerca de 1,8%.
Os dados do estudo de Fase 3, envolvendo mais de 1.100 pacientes, também mostraram que a combinação reduziu o risco de disseminação do câncer em 38%.
São os primeiros dados a demonstrar que a combinação de uma vacina baseada em mutações exclusivas do tumor de cada paciente com um medicamento que ajuda o sistema imunológico a combater o câncer pode manter a doença sob controle. A vacina foi testada em conjunto com o Keytruda, a imunoterapia de grande sucesso da MSD, que está entre os medicamentos mais vendidos do mundo.
O Keytruda atua removendo um “freio” natural que as células cancerosas usam para se esconder do ataque do sistema imunológico, enquanto a vacina instrui as células do paciente a produzir cópias de mutações específicas para que o sistema imunológico as localize e destrua.
O presidente-executivo da Moderna, Stephane Bancel, afirmou que os dados sinalizam um novo capítulo no tratamento do câncer.
“Com essa capacidade de criar novas células T específicas para o seu tumor... o impacto clínico é muito profundo e, como vimos no ensaio clínico de Fase 2, muito duradouro”, disse Bancel em uma entrevista.
As empresas estão se preparando para solicitar a aprovação nos EUA e esperam que a vacina contra o câncer seja lançada em 2027, disse Bancel.
Os resultados, baseados em dados dos pacientes relativos aos dois primeiros anos após o tratamento, devem ser apresentados no sábado, no congresso da Sociedade Europeia de Oncologia Médica, em Madri.
Entre aqueles que receberam a vacina além do Keytruda, 82,2% ainda estavam livres do câncer após dois anos, em comparação com 70% dos pacientes que receberam apenas o Keytruda.
“Isso é altamente significativo do ponto de vista estatístico. Não é por acaso”, afirmou o dr. Hussein Tawbi, especialista em melanoma e investigador do estudo no MD Anderson Cancer Center da Universidade do Texas, ao comentar os resultados.
Vários analistas de Wall Street afirmaram antes do encontro que os investidores esperavam que a combinação reduzisse o risco de recorrência em 40% ou mais.
“Parece estar ocorrendo aqui uma reação do tipo ‘compra no boato e vende no fato’”, escreveu o analista Myles Minter, da William Blair, em uma nota de pesquisa, acrescentando que as ações da Moderna acumulam alta de 525% este ano, incluindo a queda registrada nesta quinta-feira.
Minter disse que os resultados eram “ótimos dados, em nossa opinião, mas os investidores continuarão a debater a avaliação fundamental”.
O estudo testou nove doses da vacina, conhecida como intismeran, em conjunto com o Keytruda, a partir de 13 semanas após a cirurgia para remoção das lesões de melanoma. A resposta ao tratamento combinado foi comparada com a dos pacientes tratados apenas com Keytruda, uma terapia padrão para o melanoma.

items.title: Vor Bio says its experimental drug slowed loss of kidney function in late-stage study
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: US biotech company Vor Bio said on Thursday its experimental kidney disease drug slowed the loss of kidney function and reduced the risk of disease progression in a late-stage study.
items.body:
US biotech company Vor Bio (VOR.O) said on Thursday its experimental kidney disease drug slowed the loss of kidney function and reduced the risk of disease progression in a late-stage study.
The study included patients with IgA nephropathy, a disease that can eventually lead to kidney failure.
Drug telitacicept met the study's main goal and largely preserved kidney function over two years, while patients on placebo saw a steeper decline
Vor Bio said the treatment reduced the risk of a confirmed 30% decline in kidney function by 89% and the risk of a confirmed 40% decline by 81% compared with placebo
No patient receiving telitacicept reached a predefined kidney failure endpoint, compared with five patients in the placebo group, including two who required dialysis, the company said
Protein levels in urine fell 60.3% from baseline after 104 weeks while rising 0.9% in the placebo group, Vor Bio said
The company added that the reduction in protein levels was maintained after patients switched from weekly dosing to every-other-week dosing
Telitacicept received conditional approval in China in June for adults with IgA nephropathy at risk of disease progression. Vor Bio holds rights to develop and market the drug outside Greater China

Oct 22 : Olympic champion Lucas Pinheiro Braathen believes the freedom to shape his own career has allowed him to rediscover why he became a skier after the pressures of elite competition drove him to retire at the age of 23.
Braathen, who left the sport in 2023 following a dispute with the Norwegian Ski Federation, returned representing Brazil and went on to win giant slalom gold at the Milano Cortina Games, becoming the country’s first Winter Olympic champion. 
Ahead of the men’s Alpine World Cup opener in Soelden this weekend, the 26-year-old said creating an independent team had given him greater control over his sporting and commercial decisions.
“I put all the eggs in the basket of becoming the best ski racer in the world,” Braathen told Reuters in a video interview from Gurgl. “But the why was lost in that pursuit.”

Braathen won the World Cup slalom title in 2023 but announced his retirement later that year after falling out with the Norwegian federation.
He said he had faced a choice between continuing within a system that no longer reflected his ambitions and w.alking away from racing to pursue a life on his own terms.
“I could either continue skiing but put my own goals and dreams aside and be able to please the expectations of everyone around me, or I could pursue my true dream but put ski racing aside,” he said.
Braathen, who has a Brazilian mother and Norwegian father, announced his comeback in March 2024 and began competing for Brazil the following season.
SKIING IS A LIFESTYLE
His Olympic victory in February made him the first athlete from Brazil or any South American country to win a Winter Games medal. He later won last season’s giant slalom World Cup title and finished second in the overall standings.
Braathen said the control afforded by his own team also allowed him to treat commercial agreements as creative partnerships rather than conventional sponsorships.
“I don’t really approach any of my partnerships as sponsorships. I look at them as collaborations,” he said.
Atomic this week announced that it had extended its agreement with Braathen until 2030. He said his role included helping to develop equipment rather than simply endorsing the company’s products.
“For me, skiing is a lifestyle,” he said. “It’s a way of allowing people to find themselves and have an interaction with nature.”
Braathen said representing Brazil had also given his career a purpose beyond results, although he acknowledged that skiing remained beyond the reach of many people in the country.
He hopes his Olympic success can encourage Brazilians to pursue ambitions that might initially appear unrealistic and said he was working on sporting initiatives intended to create opportunities for young people.
“I hope that the fact that a Brazilian flag rose to the top of the Olympic podium covered in snow ... inspires and shows that Brazilians are truly capable of achieving whatever it is that they put their hearts and minds to,” he said.
“The harsh reality in Brazil is that many don’t have the possibility to be able to take part.”

items.author: Reuters

items.summary: Os contratos futuros de milho na bolsa de Chicago recuaram nesta quinta-feira, após atingirem mínimas de três meses no dia anterior, à medida que as negociações diplomáticas aumentaram as esperanças de uma redução da tensão na guerra da Rússia contra a Ucrânia e a colheita avançava no Meio-Oeste dos EUA.
items.body:
Os contratos futuros de milho na bolsa de Chicago recuaram nesta quinta-feira, após atingirem mínimas de três meses no dia anterior, à medida que as negociações diplomáticas aumentaram as esperanças de uma redução da tensão na guerra da Rússia contra a Ucrânia e a colheita avançava no Meio-Oeste dos EUA.
As condições climáticas secas serão favoráveis à colheita no Meio-Oeste dos EUA até o início da próxima semana, segundo o Commodity Weather Group.
O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, recebeu o enviado dos EUA, Steve Witkoff, na quarta-feira, um dia após Witkoff se reunir com o presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, na Noruega, aumentando as esperanças de uma redução da tensão no conflito no Mar Negro, que tem afetado rotas críticas de transporte de grãos.
O milho dezembro fechou com queda de 2,75 centavos, a US$4,605 o bushel.
O trigo em Chicago também recuou pelas negociações relacionadas à Ucrânia, caindo 3,50 centavos, para US$6,2475/bushel, perto de uma mínima de três meses registrada na quarta-feira.
Já os contratos futuros de soja subiram nesta quinta-feira, uma vez que as vendas semanais para exportação dos EUA ficaram no patamar superior das expectativas do mercado, compensando a diminuição da pressão exercida pela colheita.
O Departamento de Agricultura dos Estados Unidos (USDA) informou que as vendas líquidas de soja norte-americana para exportação, na semana encerrada em 15 de outubro, totalizaram 2.841.200 toneladas métricas -- um volume significativamente acima da média das quatro semanas anteriores, mas dentro da faixa de 1.800.000 a 3.000.000 de toneladas esperada pelo mercado.
O clima mais seco no Meio-Oeste norte-americano, ao longo desta semana, acelerou a colheita -- que, segundo projeções do governo, deve resultar em grandes safras de milho e soja.
O vencimento novembro da soja fechou em alta de 7,75 centavos, a US$12,53 por bushel.
(Reportagem de Renee Hickman)

items.title: Pinheiro Braathen embraces freedom after taking unconventional path to Olympic gold
items.author: Fernando Kallas
items.creator: Fernando Kallas
items.summary: Olympic champion Lucas Pinheiro Braathen believes the freedom to shape his own career has allowed him to rediscover why he became a skier after the pressures of elite competition drove him to retire at the age of 23.
items.body:
Olympic champion Lucas Pinheiro Braathen believes the freedom to shape his own career has allowed him to rediscover why he became a skier after the pressures of elite competition drove him to retire at the age of 23.
Braathen, who left the sport in 2023 following a dispute with the Norwegian Ski Federation, returned representing Brazil and went on to win giant slalom gold at the Milano Cortina Games, becoming the country’s first Winter [USN:L8N3ZA04H TEXT:"Olympic champion"].
Ahead of the men’s Alpine World Cup opener in Soelden this weekend, the 26-year-old said creating an independent team had given him greater control over his sporting and commercial decisions.
“I put all the eggs in the basket of becoming the best ski racer in the world,” Braathen told Reuters in a video interview from Gurgl. “But the why was lost in that pursuit.”
Braathen won the World Cup slalom title in 2023 but announced his retirement later that year after falling out with the Norwegian federation.
He said he had faced a choice between continuing within a system that no longer reflected his ambitions and w.alking away from racing to pursue a life on his [USN:L8N3ZA08E TEXT:"own terms"].
“I could either continue skiing but put my own goals and dreams aside and be able to please the expectations of everyone around me, or I could pursue my true dream but put ski racing aside,” he said.
Braathen, who has a Brazilian mother and Norwegian father, announced his comeback in March 2024 and began competing for Brazil the following season.
SKIING IS A LIFESTYLE His Olympic victory in February made him the first athlete from Brazil or any South American country to win a Winter Games medal. He later won last season’s giant slalom World Cup title and finished second in the overall standings.
Braathen said the control afforded by his own team also allowed him to treat commercial agreements as creative partnerships rather than conventional [USN:L6N3ZA02V TEXT:"sponsorships"].
“I don’t really approach any of my partnerships as sponsorships. I look at them as collaborations,” he said.
Atomic this week announced that it had extended its agreement with Braathen until 2030. He said his role included helping to develop equipment rather than simply endorsing the company’s products.
“For me, skiing is a lifestyle,” he said. “It’s a way of allowing people to find themselves and have an interaction with nature.”
Braathen said [USN:L1N3WS029 TEXT:"representing Brazil"] had also given his career a purpose beyond results, although he acknowledged that skiing remained beyond the reach of many people in the country.
He hopes his Olympic success can encourage Brazilians to pursue ambitions that might initially appear unrealistic and said he was working on sporting initiatives intended to create opportunities for young people.
“I hope that the fact that a Brazilian flag rose to the top of the Olympic podium covered in snow ... inspires and shows that Brazilians are truly capable of achieving whatever it is that they put their hearts and minds to,” he said.
“The harsh reality in Brazil is that many don’t have the possibility to be able to take part.”

items.title: Paciente com Ebola na Nigéria teria contraído a doença em Uganda, diz Suíça
items.author: Clement Bonnerot, Anait Miridzhanian, Robbie Corey-Boulet
items.creator: Clement Bonnerot, Anait Miridzhanian, Robbie Corey-Boulet
items.summary: A paciente com Ebola na Nigéria, esposa de um diplomata suíço lotado em Abuja e nascida em Uganda, provavelmente contraiu a doença durante uma viagem a Uganda, afirmou comunicado do governo suíço à Reuters divulgado nesta quinta-feira.
items.body:
A paciente com Ebola na Nigéria, esposa de um diplomata suíço lotado em Abuja e nascida em Uganda, provavelmente contraiu a doença durante uma viagem a Uganda, afirmou comunicado do governo suíço à Reuters divulgado nesta quinta-feira.
A Nigéria notificou o caso -- o primeiro de Ebola no país em mais de uma década -- na terça-feira, tornando-se o quarto país africano e o mais populoso a ser afetado por um surto anunciado na República Democrática do Congo em meados de maio e que, desde então, se tornou o de propagação mais rápida já registrado.
Autoridades ugandenses afirmaram que a mulher, que adoeceu na Nigéria, havia viajado para o leste do Congo antes de passar por Uganda. Mas a Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) e a principal agência de saúde da África disseram nesta quinta-feira que não haviam recebido informações confirmadas de que a mulher tivesse viajado para o Congo.
Comunicado enviado por email pelo Departamento Federal Suíço de Relações Exteriores informou que a mulher “está internada em uma clínica particular em Abuja há cerca de uma semana com sintomas".
"Acredita-se que ela tenha contraído o vírus durante uma viagem a Uganda há cerca de duas semanas”, acrescentou.
“Seu marido está em isolamento; ele não apresentou nenhum sintoma. Ele estava viajando com a esposa quando se acredita que ela tenha contraído o Ebola.”
Uganda registrou 20 casos em maio e junho, a maioria importada do Congo, mas a Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) declarou o país livre do Ebola em agosto.
Um porta-voz do governo de Uganda não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário nesta quinta-feira.
Wessam Mankoula, funcionário do Centro Africano de Controle e Prevenção de Doenças (Africa CDC), afirmou nesta quinta-feira que Nigéria e Uganda estavam compartilhando informações para apurar os deslocamentos da paciente e a possível fonte de exposição.
“Até o momento, não há informações comprovadas de que essa paciente tenha viajado para a RDC (República Democrática do Congo)”, disse Mankoula em uma coletiva de imprensa online.
A OMS afirmou que as informações que recebeu sobre o caso não incluíam viagens para fora de Uganda.

items.title: El Niño rains batter Latin America from Mexico to Chile
items.author: Cesar Olmedo
items.creator: Cesar Olmedo
items.summary: An intensifying El Niño-linked storm season this week brought flooding to Paraguay, killed two farm workers in Argentina's cattle belt and damaged coastal communities in Peru and Mexico.
items.body:
An intensifying El Niño-linked storm season this week brought flooding to Paraguay, killed two farm workers in Argentina's cattle belt and damaged coastal communities in Peru and Mexico.
Part of a luxury condominium complex on Mexico’s Pacific coast in the tourist town of San Pancho in Nayarit State collapsed on Wednesday after pounding surf ate away the sand beneath it, exposing its foundation and leaving the structure tilted dramatically toward the sea.
In Paraguay, two dozen families took refuge late on Wednesday at a church near Paraguay's border with Brazil after their homes flooded and more residents anxiously watched the swelling [USN:L4N2QW4DD TEXT:"Parana"], South America's second-largest river, as rains battered the region.
UN officials [USN:L6N4670T1 TEXT:"warned"] this week that the El Niño weather pattern could drive a record increase in Pacific Ocean temperatures as it moves around the globe like a "wrecking ball," triggering floods in some regions and droughts in others.
In Paraguay, the rising Parana River, a key commercial waterway, has affected about 4,200 families, according to the country's national emergency agency.
A 58-year-old woman died after her home collapsed in the rains.
At the church now doubling as a shelter, in Paraguay's Ciudad del Este, dozens of residents pitched tents on a soccer field while others organized communal kitchens with support from the church and local businesses.
In San Rafael, a riverside town, Antonina Sánchez, 65, recounted how she had to flee.
"I was surprised because the water came very quickly. My house, my entire kitchen collapsed; it's caving in," she said.
The World Meteorological Organization has predicted temperatures in the central Pacific will rise about 3.8 degrees Celsius above average between November and January, peaking around December, causing one of the most turbulent storm seasons on record.
RAIN, HAIL, MUD AND EROSION Elsewhere in Latin America this week, two farm workers died near Bella Vista in Argentina's Corrientes province while moving cattle away from flooded areas near the Parana, local media reported.
Hundreds of residents have been evacuated across the province, though above-average rainfall in parts of the Pampas agricultural belt could [USN:L6N42J17M TEXT:"benefit crops"].
In Chile's capital Santiago, a flooded stream triggered a mudslide on October 8 onto city streets, and days later, a storm blanketed roads with hail and flooded streets.
In Peru, authorities on Thursday announced [USN:L1N4680UE TEXT:"financial aid"] and tax relief for businesses affected by extreme weather battering the country's Pacific coast. The government plans to allocate 18 billion soles ($5.22 billion) in 2027 towards mitigating the economic impact.

items.title: Trump pede a Musk que suspenda as restrições à Starlink na Ucrânia, diz WSJ
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ligou para Elon Musk e pediu que ele suspenda as restrições ao uso da Starlink pela Ucrânia, informou o Wall Street Journal nesta quinta-feira, citando autoridades norte-americanas.
items.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ligou para Elon Musk e pediu que ele suspenda as restrições ao uso da Starlink pela Ucrânia, informou o Wall Street Journal nesta quinta-feira, citando autoridades norte-americanas.
O sistema Starlink estava funcionando de maneira mais normal nesta quinta-feira, logo após a conversa entre Trump e Musk, segundo autoridades norte-americanas e ucranianas citadas pelo Journal.
Algumas autoridades ucranianas disseram ao jornal que o sistema não havia recuperado sua funcionalidade total, mas estava operando em velocidades mais altas do que aquelas limitadas anteriormente.
O presidente Volodymyr Zelenskiy havia dito na manhã desta quinta-feira que a velocidade do Starlink ainda não havia sido restaurada para a Ucrânia, acrescentando que esperava manter conversas com o secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, nos próximos dias.
Trump disse a Musk que estava frustrado porque as velocidades do sistema continuavam limitadas a cerca de 160 km/h, informou o Journal, citando autoridades.
Rubio disse na quarta-feira que as decisões relativas ao acesso da Ucrânia à Starlink cabiam à empresa controladora SpaceX e ao seu presidente-executivo, Musk, e não à Casa Branca.
A Ucrânia utiliza a Starlink para comunicações no campo de batalha e operações com drones. A restrição ao serviço de satélite prejudicou as missões de ataque e de defesa aérea com drones do país contra a Rússia.

items.title: SpaceX says potential Tesla merger would need Elon Musk's approval
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: SpaceX said on Thursday its potential merger with Tesla will require controlling investor Elon Musk's approval, even though the entrepreneur has recused himself from talks between his two companies because of conflicts of interest.
items.body:
SpaceX (SPCX.O) said on Thursday its potential merger with Tesla (TSLA.O) will require controlling investor Elon Musk's approval, even though the entrepreneur has recused himself from talks between his two companies because of conflicts of interest.
Musk, the world's richest person, said on Tuesday [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"a merger of SpaceX and Tesla would be "a good idea""] and that they had formed special committees to discuss a union.
In a regulatory filing on Thursday, SpaceX said, "No determination by our special committee has been made regarding any potential combination, and any potential combination would be subject to further approval by our special committee, our board of directors and our controlling shareholder."
Several Wall Street analysts have said they see a Tesla-SpaceX merger as a matter of when, not if, but disagree on how much Tesla shareholders should receive in a deal.
Musk's public endorsement this week of the potential $3.5 trillion merger has also rattled some insiders involved in the discussions, who worry his comments could invite shareholder scrutiny and delay the process by several weeks, [USN:L6N46716H TEXT:"Reuters reported"] earlier on Thursday.
Musk owns nearly a fifth of Tesla and holds voting control at SpaceX. Analysts have said a merger would give him control of the combined entity and could consolidate his influence.
The disclosure created a "mess" for the process, as it could lead to questions about how well Tesla shareholders' interests would be represented, a person with direct knowledge of the talks told Reuters.
Bringing the companies together [USN:L1N46701K TEXT:"could also simplify decision-making"], as multiple companies require approvals from separate boards and shareholders. The potential merger could give management the flexibility to allocate capital, engineering talent and infrastructure toward more promising projects as firms aggressively push into AI.
Tesla on Wednesday cut its annual [USN:L4N4671SD TEXT:"capital expenditure forecast to roughly $20 billion"], down from its previous forecast of more than $25 billion. SpaceX [USN:L4N4661M0 TEXT:"expects $35 billion to $40 billion"] in capital expenditure in the fourth quarter.
SpaceX is a major contractor for the US military, intelligence agencies and NASA. Tesla, meanwhile, remains deeply tied to China through its Shanghai factory, which plays a major role in vehicle production and sales.
Shares of SpaceX rose about 1%, while those of Tesla fell marginally in extended trading.

items.title: Peso mexicano cae tras datos locales de inflación, bolsa se repliega
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El peso mexicano retrocedió el jueves arrastrado por un débil entorno para los activos de riesgo ante persistentes tensiones en Medio Oriente y después de conocerse que la inflación local se aceleró en la primera quincena de octubre más de lo esperado.
items.body:
El peso mexicano retrocedió el jueves arrastrado por un débil entorno para los activos de riesgo ante persistentes tensiones en [USN:L6N4680XU TEXT:"Medio Oriente"] y después de conocerse que la [USN:L1N4680NW TEXT:"inflación local"] se aceleró en la primera quincena de octubre más de lo esperado.
Los datos redujeron las apuestas a que Banco de México podría recortar su tasa clave, coincidieron analistas. El mercado, sin embargo, mantiene las expectativas de una pausa monetaria prolongada, incluso si la Reserva Federal vuelve a elevar los tipos de interés.
* La moneda local cotizaba en 18.7110 unidades por dólar en la recta final de los negocios, con una depreciación de un 0.22%, también golpeada por renovadas preocupaciones sobre el suministro global de [USN:L1N46812A TEXT:"petróleo"] ante un recrudecimiento de la violencia en Arabia Saudita.
* Antes de conocerse la inflación local, el peso llegó a debilitarse hasta 18.8550 por dólar, un nivel no visto desde septiembre de 2025, pero luego moderó las pérdidas, ya que el repunte de los precios al consumidor complicó las perspectivas de un recorte a la tasa de interés referencial.
* La posibilidad de una rebaja de tasas había cobrado fuerza después de que la minuta de la última reunión del banco central reveló que tres de los cinco miembros de la [USN:L1N45U0OW TEXT:"Junta de Gobierno"] se mostraron abiertos a una mayor flexibilización monetaria si ceden las presiones inflacionarias.
* El mercado, no obstante, mantiene vigentes las previsiones de que [USN:L6N45G177 TEXT:"Banco de México"] dejaría los tipos de interés sin cambios hasta finales de 2027, aun cuando la [USN:L1N4580T6 TEXT:"Reserva Federal"] podría volver a elevarlos a finales de este año, después de su alza de septiembre.
* "Las perspectivas actuales de inflación y las presiones externas deberían llevar al Banxico a mantener su postura sin cambios en el futuro previsible", dijo Barclays.
* La plaza accionaria también registró una jornada negativa presionada por un ajuste de posiciones después de cinco sesiones continuas de ganancias, que la llevaron a alcanzar el miércoles su mayor nivel de cierre [USN:L1N467010 TEXT:"desde abril"].
* El referencial índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) cedió un 0.51% a 69,889.73 puntos, mientras los inversionistas vigilan de cerca los reportes corporativos locales del tercer trimestre.
* Los títulos de Gentera (GENTERA.MX) , especializada en microcréditos, encabezaron las bajas, con un 6.32% menos a 37.81 pesos, su mayor descalabro diario desde junio de 2024.
* Analistas dijeron que si bien la compañía divulgó cifras trimestrales mejores a lo estimado, un [USN:L1N4680SF TEXT:"incremento de la morosidad"] alimentó preocupaciones sobre la calidad de sus activos.
* Las acciones mineras también cayeron, siguiendo un descenso de los [USN:L1N4680Z3 TEXT:"precios de los metales"]. Grupo México (GMEXICOB.MX) perdió un 4.34% a 231.36 pesos, mientras que Industrias Peñoles (PEOLES.MX) retrocedió un 3.50% a 856.33 pesos.
* Durante su [USN:L1N468173 TEXT:"llamada con analistas"], ejecutivos de Grupo México dijeron que se prevén inversiones de capital por hasta 6,000 millones de dólares en los principales proyectos de su unidad estadounidense Asarco durante los próximos tres años.
* En el mercado secundario de deuda, el rendimiento del bono gubernamental a 10 años descendió dos puntos base a un 9.26%, mientras que la tasa a 20 años subió uno, a un 9.75%.

items.title: When should a judge's social life be grounds for a do-over?
items.author: Jenna Greene
items.creator: Jenna Greene
items.summary: A group of lawyers and retired judges are warning that the social lives of US magistrate and bankruptcy judges could be unfairly picked apart by losing litigants seeking a do-over, as a federal appeals court grapples with how much judges must reveal about their friendships with the lawyers who appear before them.
items.body:
A group of lawyers and retired judges are warning that the social lives of US magistrate and bankruptcy judges could be unfairly picked apart by losing litigants seeking a do-over, as a federal appeals court grapples with how much judges must reveal about their friendships with the lawyers who appear before them.
Arising from a contract dispute over a ship canal in Lake Charles, Louisiana, [USN:L1N4500V6 TEXT:"the case"] hinges on undisclosed social ties between a now-retired magistrate judge and a lawyer whose client she awarded $125 million.
The 5th US Circuit Court of Appeals on Thursday withdrew an opinion it issued last month that wiped out the award. The New Orleans-based court granted a rare rehearing and said a new opinion would be issued, but gave no hint if the outcome would change. No additional briefing or oral argument was requested.
The sharply divided panel ruled 2-1 in September that US Magistrate Judge Kathleen Kay should have revealed more up front about her longstanding ties with the lawyer, including that he was a groomsman in her wedding 30 years ago.
Because she did not fully disclose the relationship, the panel held that the Port of Lake Charles could withdraw its consent for her to decide the case – even though it sought to do so only after losing a 20-day bench trial.
Kay did not respond to a request for comment, nor did the Port or its outside counsel, Michael Rubin of Adams & Reese.
Lawyers for the Port’s opponent, terminal operator IFG Port Holdings, which saw its $125 million win stripped away, argue that the decision invites copycat moves, creating a “roadmap for invalidating countless final judgments.”
Disappointed litigants now need only “proffer ignorance of a potential conflict — no matter how unjustified — to obtain a second bite at the apple,” IFG’s lawyers from Latham & Watkins argued in urging the court to reconsider the case.
“It’s an issue of exceptional importance,” Latham partner Gregory Garre said.
The plaintiffs are backed by six retired judges, who in an amicus brief filed Tuesday warned that the new standard would prove unworkable in practice, especially in smaller legal communities like Lake Charles, where professional and social ties among members of the bar are plentiful.
Inevitably, a judge “may fail to disclose a tangential connection that losing parties then seize on,” judges W. Royal Furgeson, Jr, Mildred Methvin, Brian Owsley, Viktor Pohorelsky, Stephen Wm. Smith and Judith Fitzgerald wrote.
EXTRAORDINARY CIRCUMSTANCES? There are about 600 magistrate judges and 300 bankruptcy judges nationwide — more than the number of federal district and circuit judges combined, and they play an essential role in managing the federal docket.
Unlike Senate-confirmed Article III judges who are appointed for life by the US president, magistrate and bankruptcy judges are chosen via a merit-based hiring process and serve a set term. Magistrates handle much of a court’s pretrial work, while bankruptcy judges oversee cases ranging from individual debtors to complex restructurings.
Their authority has limits. In some cases, the judges can only decide disputes with the parties' knowing and voluntary consent. However, once that permission is given, Congress by statute has said it may only be withdrawn “under extraordinary circumstances.”
What exactly this means is key to the Fifth Circuit case.
The litigation, which concerned dredging a ship canal at the industrial port, began in 2016. When the parties agreed to a bench trial before Kay, she disclosed at the outset that IFG’s lead counsel William Monk’s daughter, Margaret, was her law clerk and would be screened from the matter.
Monk did not respond to a request for comment.
After Kay ruled against the port in 2020 in a sharply worded, 64-page opinion, two wives of lawyers on the losing side did some social media sleuthing. Or, as Judge Andrew Oldham put it in his dissent, “Facebook-stalking.”
They found photos of Kay’s wedding in 1989 that showed Monk as a groomsman, and posts of Kay officiating the wedding of Monk’s other daughter, Lucie, in 2015.
“If the Port had knowledge of the full extent of the relationship between the Magistrate Judge and Plaintiff's counsel, it would not have consented to the referral,” lawyers for the Port wrote in a bare-bones motion in 2020 asking that the case be taken away from Kay and her decision vacated.
After an initial review by the Fifth Circuit in 2023, the matter was remanded to Judge Michael Truncale in Beaumont, Texas (the entire Western District of Louisiana was recused) to [USN:L1N3AX2H4 TEXT:"conduct an inquiry"] into the friendship.
Truncale cataloged casual social interactions between Kay and Monk spanning decades, from playing Trivial Pursuit together in the 1980s to attending the same annual Christmas party to sitting together at a fundraising dinner. Kay and Monk's wife were childhood acquaintances, and the couples' sons were also friends.
While Kay testified that she did not consider Monk to be a friend of hers, just a friend of her husband’s, Truncale found the “existence of a close, family friendship spanning nearly forty years.”
IFG’s lawyers question whether the port was truly unaware of the bond. For example, the Port’s general counsel “liked” Kay’s Facebook post that included the photo of Monk as a groomsman.
Moreover, Port lawyer Rick Norman of Taylor Porter and his wife attended the wedding of Kay’s daughter in 2017 — and allegedly walked into the ceremony with fellow invitees the Monks.
The Fifth Circuit majority held that evidence suggesting the Port was aware Kay and Monk were socially acquainted was not enough. Rather, a party must "actually know the nature and extent" of any potential conflict in order to consent to proceed before a magistrate judge.
A litigant's “constructive knowledge” — information it should have inferred from the circumstances or could have discovered through reasonable diligence — is not sufficient, the panel held.
The appeals court could strengthen its findings or rethink them as it rehears the case. Its decision could clarify where judges should draw the line between ordinary social relationships and connections that must be disclosed to litigants, lest the losing side seize on the ties to unravel a case.
items.raw_description: A group of lawyers and retired judges are warning that the social lives of US magistrate and bankruptcy judges could be unfairly picked apart by losing litigants seeking a do-over, as a federal appeals court grapples with how much judges must reveal about their friendships with the lawyers who appear before them.

items.title: James Hoye named umpiring crew chief for Rays-Brewers World Series
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Veteran umpire James Hoye was named crew chief for the 2026 World Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers, Major League Baseball announced on Thursday.
items.body:
Veteran umpire James Hoye was named crew chief for the 2026 World Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers, Major League Baseball announced on Thursday.
Hoye, 55, will be an umpire in the World Series for the third time and this will be his first Fall Classic as a crew chief. He was also part of World Series crews in 2019 and 2022. Hoye has been a full-time MLB ump since 2010.
The other umpires appointed to the World Series crew are Dan Bellino, Vic Carapazza, Tripp Gibson, Nic Lentz, Gabe Morales and Jim Wolf. Bellino, Carapazza and Hoye are crew chiefs during the regular season.
MLB said having seven umpires allows for "distinct home plate assignments in a potential seven-game series." One umpire will be off the field for each game. Bellino will serve as crew chief when Hoye is off the field in Game 3.
Wolf (2015, 2019) is working his third World Series, while Bellino (2021), Carapazza (2023) and Gibson (2022) are working their second. Lentz and Morales are working their first World Series.
Umpires Alfonso Marquez, a regular-season crew chief, and D.J. Reyburn have been assigned to assist with replays.
Game 1 is Friday night in Milwaukee.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Newmont beats quarterly profit estimates on higher gold prices, Cadia recovery
items.author: Varun Sahay, Divya Rajagopal
items.creator: Varun Sahay, Divya Rajagopal
items.summary: Newmont beat analysts' third-quarter profit estimates on Thursday, as elevated gold prices and a recovery in copper production at its Cadia mine in Australia boosted earnings.
items.body:
Newmont (NEM.N) beat analysts' third-quarter profit estimates on Thursday, as elevated gold prices and a recovery in copper production at its Cadia mine in Australia boosted earnings.
Gold prices averaged $4,204.59 per ounce during the quarter, up about 17.6% from a year earlier, as investors sought safe-haven assets despite a stronger dollar and inflation concerns tied to higher oil prices during the US war on Iran.
Quarterly revenue rose 15% to $6.36 billion, while copper production jumped 35% from the previous quarter to 23,000 tonnes as Cadia recovered from a prior-quarter disruption.
Shares of the company were up 1.5% in extended trading.
Newmont said it was advancing its Red Chris Block Cave joint venture in the British Columbia province of Canada toward a final investment decision in early 2027.
The project is expected to produce about 3 million ounces of gold and more than 850,000 tonnes of copper over an initial 13-year cave life. Commercial production is targeted for 2033.
The miner, which owns 70% of Red Chris, estimated development capital at $4.2 billion to $4.8 billion, net of an anticipated C$500 million ($356.99 million) contribution from the Canadian government.
The company also amended its Nevada Gold Mines joint-venture agreement with Canada's Barrick Mining (ABX.TO) to include Barrick's Fourmile and Newmont's Fiberline and Mike properties, and plans to pay Barrick $1.95 billion in the fourth quarter.
CEO Natascha Viljoen said Newmont was not interested in bidding for Australian gold miner Northern Star Resources (NST.AX) , saying its assets did not align with the company's strategy.
"It is really hard to find anything better than what we have internally in our own operations," Viljoen said.
The company posted adjusted profit of $2.20 per share for the quarter ended September 30, above analysts' average estimate of $2.05 per share, according to data compiled by LSEG.
($1 = 1.4006 Canadian dollars)

items.title: Giants OC: J.J. McCarthy's skill set opens up more of playbook
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Having J.J. McCarthy as the starting quarterback allows the New York Giants to run nearly the entire offense they installed during the preseason, when Jaxson Dart was the starter, offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said Thursday.
items.body:
Having J.J. McCarthy as the starting quarterback allows the New York Giants to run nearly the entire offense they installed during the preseason, when Jaxson Dart was the starter, offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said Thursday.
Like Dart, McCarthy is a mobile quarterback. With McCarthy now in the starting role, Nagy can restore most of the elements that were removed when the Giants replaced Dart with veteran pocket passer Jameis Winston following Dart's season-ending knee injury last month.
"I think for us, and I know for us going into this thing, knowing what we wanted to do with Jaxson's ability and his traits, him and Jameis are very different, and that's OK. Now, coming into this thing with J.J., you get to a point where his skill set is very similar to Jaxson," Nagy said. "So, it's like, OK, it brings back -- we talked about percentages the first time we were here, right? You talked about whether it's 30 percent of the offense is gone. Well, maybe now 20 percent of that 30 that was gone is back."
The Giants (3-2-1) benched Winston in favor of McCarthy on Sunday after falling behind 34-10 against the New Orleans Saints. McCarthy led three scoring drives in the fourth quarter against New Orleans' prevent defense before driving New York to the Saints' 14-yard line in the final seconds. The Giants turned the ball over on downs to end the rally.
The third-year pro completed 11 of 21 passes for 234 yards, with one touchdown and one interception. He also rushed for 26 yards on two carries.
"When you're down 24 points, they're going to naturally, most defenses, play a little bit more prevent/soft defense. We understand that, but there's still a lot of throws within that game in the fourth quarter where he made some really impressive throws," Nagy said.
McCarthy's ability to throw and run gives Nagy more options. Previously, when McCarthy entered as Winston's backup, defenses could anticipate a quarterback run.
"Now that he's the quarterback and the starter, it probably benefits us some that he's just not always coming in to do predictable QB-driven runs," Nagy said.
McCarthy is still learning the offense after the Giants acquired him from the Minnesota Vikings for a 2027 fifth-round draft pick on Sept. 28. New York brought in the 2024 first-round pick (10th overall) after Dart's injury.
McCarthy will face his first true test Sunday when the Giants travel to Houston to take on the Texans (2-4), who are coming off a 34-31 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Kevin Kisner sees Tiger Woods targeting Masters with TGL slate, Hero
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: NBC Sports lead golf analyst Kevin Kisner said he foresees Tiger Woods using his play in TGL as a springboard to more competitive golf in 2027.
items.body:
NBC Sports lead golf analyst Kevin Kisner said he foresees Tiger Woods using his play in TGL as a springboard to more competitive golf in 2027.
It was announced earlier this week that Woods will compete for the Jupiter Links GC entry in TGL, the winter golf simulator league, with Woods taking Kisner's spot.
Kisner, who is also a part-time player on the PGA Tour, said on a recent podcast that he was told Woods wanted to play a full schedule.
"Rob (McNamara), Tiger's guy, he texted me a long text last week, I think, just telling me what they did on their decisions, how they were moving around and what players are going to do," Kisner said on the Barstool "Fore Play" episode posted Wednesday.
Injuries, legal issues and time in a Swiss rehabilitation center earlier this year have kept Woods, 50, from playing in a pro tournament since The Open Championship in 2024.
Kisner said he anticipates Woods will play in the Hero World Challenge (Dec. 3-6), which he hosts in the Bahamas, and the PNC Championship (Dec. 19-20). If that goes well, he could target the Masters (April 8-11).
He missed the PNC last year because of back surgery, but he typically plays in that family event with his son, Charlie.
"He can't have any more setbacks injury-wise, but the way he was swinging and moving on the range, the guy loves to compete," Kisner said. "Come back, get your feet wet at the Hero, play with Charlie at the father-son, play some TGL, get ready for Augusta."
--Field Level Media
